News.title: Arsenal maintain perfect start but lack firepower of rivals
News.content:
Bukayo Saka maintained Arsenal’s perfect start to the season, but Mikel Arteta appeared to acknowledge that the Premier League champions are in danger of leaving themselves short in attack.

There is still time for Arteta to add another forward to his squad and whether he does so or not could be important, with the transfer window closing on Tuesday night.

Having sold Leandro Trossard and with Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus on the verge of moves away, Arsenal appear light of forward options.

Lyon winger Malick Fofana has been offered to the club, but he is an underwhelming target given Morgan Rogers and Vinícius Júnior were pursued earlier in the summer.

“We are trying to improve the squad,” Arteta, the Arsenal head coach, said. “Until Tuesday night, we’re going to try to do that. I’ve been disconnected from the world for 24 hours because I think my energy and focus has to be on the match. I will give it [my energy] now.”

Asked if he currently has enough depth in forward positions, Arteta added: “It depends if everybody is fit or not. We know that the depth has to be really big when you are fighting for four competitions. So we’re going to try to do that.”

News.title: Manchester United’s attack may be their best form of defence this season
News.content:
Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick in what was another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

In the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “new signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

News.title: Robinson’s Victorian-style bowling figures secure series victory over Pakistan
News.content:
The only missing aspect was a five-fer which would have brought a 100th Test wicket. Even so, his career average is now 19.53, the best for England since Frank Tyson of those with 50 or more wickets.

Mr Nude Nuts, as Matthew Hayden called him, could be devastating against Australia and, like Root the captain, deserves to be judged on what happens in his second incarnation rather than what went before.

Robinson’s pace has lingered around the 79mph mark and inevitably that throws up Rob Key’s assertion you cannot succeed in Test cricket bowling in the 70s with the keeper standing up. Key was referring to county bowlers pitching it up and relying on the Dukes ball to do the rest.

It was thrown in his face in Australia but Michael Neser and Scott Boland are not county trundlers: they extract more energy off the pitch than that.

Robinson is also no dobber. His high release point combined with a mastery of length means he is always threatening the top of off stump. He also knows which way the ball is going to nip, giving no clues to the batsmen due to his sleight of hand skills.

With Jamie Smith improving under the tutelage of Sarah Taylor, he can operate with the keeper standing up which pins batsmen in the crease, bringing all modes of dismissals into play. Robinson was as effective with the new ball as the old: his two seven-over spells were two for 13 and two for 11.

How snarling Robinson adds edge and precision

At 32, he has become a combination of Stuart Broad and James Anderson, although down on their pace with the height and bounce of the former, and tricks of the latter. He can move the new ball further either way than Anderson or Broad but the question is whether he has their durability and sheer competitiveness.

He has not been tested this summer by pitches or opponents. He has not bowled more than 18 overs in an innings and was injured when England played on the best batting pitch at the Oval. He was not trusted at Trent Bridge because the old management had burned their fingers before. That decision may well have cost the coach his job.

Like Broad and Anderson he has a snarl too, sending Abdullah Shafique on his way with a word or two. There was no need for that but maybe it was just a carried away reaction to bowling an absolute beauty that angled in, seamed away and hit the top of off.

News.title: Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness
News.content:
Xabi Alonso takes charge of his first home Premier League game in charge of Chelsea as they host Brighton at Stamford Bridge. Both sides were in action in two different competitions on Thursday night. Chelsea reached the League Cup third round as they beat Luton 2-0 at Stamford Bridge, with former Brighton man Danny Welbeck scoring on his debut. Brighton meanwhile confirmed their place in the Conference League group stages with a 4-0 aggregate win over Tromso.

Chelsea began their Premier League campaign last Monday in a west London derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage, winning 3-2 in Alonso’s first game as Chelsea boss. Enzo Fernandez was not involved in Chelsea’s squad against Luton on Thursday and has been heavily linked with a move to Manchester City. Alonso was asked about Enzo’s absence on Thursday and did not confirm whether the Argentine would be involved today.

“It was just because of the game today [on Thursday] and we have other players who need minutes,” Alonso said. “[On Wednesday], in the afternoon. It is a decision that I took. Enzo is a good professional. He is training well and I have nothing to say about this. It was just decisions that we have to take thinking about the game that we were playing tonight [Thursday]. We will see for Sunday [today].”

Brighton began their Premier League campaign in emphatic style as they thrashed Aston Villa 4-0 at home seven days ago. Jack Hinshelwood scored twice in that game but will now miss a number of weeks with an ankle injury. They are also without Yankuba Minteh, who has been linked with a move to Liverpool this summer but is unavailable due to injury.

“When the window is closed I demand from him [Minteh] that he is fully committed to this club,” Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said. “There are dreams and wishes for players, but in the end we always need to figure out what is best for the club.

“We have had an exchange with him. At the moment he is definitely a Brighton player. It is very important to understand his thoughts but also our planning. As a club we try to develop players. The last few years have shown that the whole environment gave him a lot of trust and belief that he is capable of having this progress. It is always a give and take and he has gotten a lot from us.”

Brighton won both Premier League meetings last season, winning 3-1 in this fixture last September. Brighton have won five of their last eight top-flight meetings with Chelsea. Team news from Stamford Bridge to follow shortly.

Sports.title: David Moyes facing battle to even fill Everton’s bench each week after disastrous end to transfer window
Sports.content:
DAVID MOYES faces a battle to even fill his substitutes’ bench following a disastrous end to the transfer window for Everton.

The Toffees managed to recruit Jack Grealish and Ainsley Maitland-Niles on deadline day, but these incomings were overshadowed by other business.



Everton sold talisman Iliman Ndiaye to Manchester City, in addition to flogging Nathan Patterson to Torino, Tim Iroegbunam to Hull and Beto to Fiorentina.

The latter departure could prove to be particularly costly, with a last-gasp move for replacement Folarin Balogun falling through.



Everton had agreed a £40million deal for the Monaco striker earlier in the day, only for an issue with the medical to throw the move into doubt.

The Toffees went back in for Balogun after a late swoop for Joshua Zirkzee failed, and even managed to agree a lower fee.

Moyes’ men submitted a deal sheet to get the signing through beyond the deadline… only for Balogun himself to pull the plug.

This means that following Beto’s exit, Thierno Barry is the only senior striker available to Moyes.



Beto had come off the bench in Everton’s opening two Premier League matches of the season, but the Toffees will now no longer have this option.

Everton also failed with a bid for Tottenham star Richarlison, the Brazilian subsequently releasing an explosive statement on social media after the switch failed to materialise.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Things could have gotten even worse for the Toffees, had they sold promising academy graduate Harrison Armstrong.

Club chiefs had agreed a £40m deal to sell the 19-year-old to Nottingham Forest, only to perform a U-turn amid a fan revolt.

Even with Armstrong still in tow, Moyes has just a 21-man senior squad to choose from.



This means that just one injury would force to the Scot to name two goalkeepers as substitutes, should he want to fill his bench with senior pros.

Moyes pleaded not to be left short after Saturday’s 1-1 draw at Bournemouth.

The experienced boss said last week: “For us to be a side which is competitive, we have still got a lot of work to do. Hopefully we are able to try to do some of it. We need more players.



“Our squad is not big enough and we need to get more quality in some areas, if we can do.

“I’m not sure we will, but it’s not for me and the want of trying, that’s for sure.”

Everton fans were understandably left fuming with their club’s end to the transfer window.

One wrote on X: “Someone needs to answer for this utter negligence but we’ll get nothing as usual”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And a second raged: “The incompetence of this is absolutely insane”.



Another added: “It’s unacceptable and a lack of respect to the fans, players and manager.”

Sports.title: Enzo Fernandez is £125m risk for Man City, he ruffled feathers at Chelsea, has bad temperament and preferred Real Madrid
Sports.content:
MONTHS of flirting, weeks of briefing and dubious deadlines coming and going – all on top of a British record-equalling fee.

But is Enzo Fernandez worth all of the fuss?



The fiery Argentina midfielder arrived in January 2023 for a then British record £106million and is yet to prove he is worth that, let alone the £125m Manchester City will pay.

Fernandez has delivered some significant moments in a Chelsea shirt, but has also caused them all manner of issues they could have done without.



His goal against Paris Saint-Germain, in the first leg of their Champions League last-16 tie, told the full story. Fernandez pointed to the Club World Cup winners’ badge – won with a win over the Parisians in America – after equalising at Parc Des Princes.

Chelsea went on to lose 5-2 on the night and 8-2 on aggregate.

Enzo Maresca knows the quality the former Benfica man can bring once the whistle goes, but before he had even met him had to wrestle with off-field misdemeanors.

Following Argentina’s 2024 Copa America triumph, Fernandez live streamed celebrations from the team bus. Those celebrations included him and his teammates singing a derogatory chant which dated back to the 2022 World Cup, aimed at French players of African descent.

Chelsea’s touring squad that summer, which featured Frenchmen Wesley Fofana, Axel Disasi, Benoit Badiashile, Christopher Nkunku and Malo Gusto, were less than impressed.

Maresca’s unveiling press conference in California was dominated by difficult questions about a midfielder he had not worked with yet and one who, eventually, joined the squad early in Atlanta and, tail between his legs, needed to apologise. It was quite the clean-up job.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Fernandez and Maresca went on to form a close bond, with the Italian’s departure on New Year’s Day the seed of his discontent which led to his open flirting with Real Madrid and talk of a Stamford Bridge exit which started in March.

Madrid was Fernandez’s preferred destination this summer, but once the Spanish giants made it clear – in an unusual public statement – that they would not be pursuing a deal this summer, the focus turned to a reunion with Maresca in Manchester.

The midfielder’s agitation to leave certainly ruffled feathers at Chelsea and should serve as a warning signal to his new employers.

Fernandez spent just six months at Benfica before a December World Cup accelerated his move to Chelsea and he was happy to move on.

What is to say that, after 18 months at The Etihad, his eyes do not turn to Madrid once more and City are left dealing with the sort of saga Chelsea have had to manage for the past six months. No one agrees a record fee to try and spin a player for profit within two years.



The unsettling work of Fernandez’s interviews on international duty and the public assertions of his agent, former Argentina and Paris Saint-Germain man Javier Pastore, set him back at Chelsea. He was given credit for working hard for the rest of the season, but those missteps were described as countless self-inflicted wounds, but ones which could be healed had he committed to the club.

New manager Xabi Alonso made it clear he wanted the 2022 World Cup winner to stay at Stamford Bridge having spoken to him shortly after his appointment on July 1. But that stance has since softened and, after Fernandez was booed by a section of Blues fans, he made a substitute appearance in the opening Premier League game at Fulham and has not been in a squad since.

Chelsea’s ill-discipline has been evident for at least the past two seasons. Before even arriving at Cobham, Alonso identified a need to address the dressing room culture and clear out some bad apples. Fernandez played a significant part in the club’s record breaking discipline record.

RECOMMENDED STORIES



His sending off in the World Cup final, the first booking being for dissent, was taken as confirmation that there was a serious temperament problem.

Maresca’s ability to calm this firebrand will be the deciding factor in whether City get value for money or not.

Sports.title: Most expensive Premier League transfers ever after inflation with Enzo Fernandez’s £125m Man City move not in top 20
Sports.content:
ENZO FERNANDEZ made a blockbuster move to Manchester City on deadline day – but changing spending power means he is not even in the Premier League’s top 20 most expensive signings.

The Argentine, 25, quit Chelsea for the Etihad Stadium in a record-equalling £125million deal.



It matched the fee that Liverpool forked out to tempt Newcastle into flogging Alexander Isak last year.

But, sensationally, neither of them would be anywhere near being crowned the English top-flight’s most lucrative recruit if inflation and changing spending powers are taken into account.



Football finance expert Kieran Maguire reports Alan Shearer’s £15m move to Newcastle in 1996 equates to a whopping £238.3M in today’s money.

And that would make the England legend, who is still the all-time leading goalscorer in Premier League history, the most expensive addition by a huge margin.



Juan Sebastian Veron would be second on the list following his arrival at Manchester United in 2001.

Although the Red Devils agreed a fee of £28.1m at the time, it would look more like an eye-watering £185.1m if he made the switch in the current financial climate.

Stan Collymore’s £8.5m move from Nottingham Forest to Liverpool seems to be a bargain on the surface.

But, when changing spending powers are taken into consideration, he headed to Anfield for what is now £179.3m.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Six-time Premier League champion Rio Ferdinand features in the top 20 TWICE.

The England legend joined Man Utd for what is £174.8m in today’s money – making him the fourth most expensive acquisition.

And he also bags 12th spot after swapping West Ham for Leeds in November 2000.

Romelu Lukaku, who sealed a switch to Fenerbahce last month, is found in 14th and 18th place following his arrivals at Man Utd and Chelsea respectively.

Andy Cole, Wayne Rooney, Paul Pogba, Dwight Yorke and Angel Di Maria make the top 20 thanks to their moves to Old Trafford.



They are joined by Fernando Torres, Andriy Shevchenko, Moises Caicedo, Didier Drogba and Michael Essien, who embarked on a fresh challenge at Chelsea.

Dennis Bergkamp is the only Arsenal representative as his arrival from Inter Milan is now worth a stunning £158.2m.

Faustino Asprilla and Jack Grealish, who made a deadline day loan move to Everton, are also in the top 20 as a result of being nabbed by Newcastle and Man City respectively.

Sports.title: Shocking moment fan invades pitch and attacks his own team as goalkeeper retaliates and riot police charge on
Sports.content:
A URUGUAYAN football match was marred by bizarre scenes after a fan invaded the pitch to attack his OWN team.

Top flight sides Torque and Danubio were in action in the Copa Uruguay when the match had to be halted temporarily.



Footage shows three supporters jumping the railings and storming onto the pitch mid-game.

One fan sprints towards a group of Danubio players and immediately starts pushing two of them.



The scenes then turned into chaos as the Danubio goalkeeper ran all the way to the half line to confront the pitch invader.

The keeper shoved the fan and chased after him before striking him on the head and grappling with him.

One of his team-mates then grabs him to stop him from harming the fan and ends up tackling him to the ground.

The situation sparked a huge melee as both teams attempted to corner the pitch invader and get him off the field of play.

Fans were thrilled by the goalkeeper’s quick-thinking and decisive behaviour in chasing the fan off the pitch.

One said on Reddit: “Keeper went straight to DEFCON 1, fair play.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

A second added: “Always the goalkeeper, they are just built different. I love them.”

A third wrote: “Goalkeeper was waiting for this moment his entire life!”

Others criticised the fan for attacking his own players.



One added: “You’re not a fan when you attack your own players.”

Another said: “I will never understand people that take sports to that level. It’s indefensible.”

Danubio went on to lose the game 2-0 to Torque in the Copa Uruguay group stage to leave them with three points from two games.

Sports.title: Man Utd have highest net spend in last decade despite Chelsea splashing nearly £1billion MORE than rivals
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED have the highest net spend in world football over the last decade, despite Chelsea handing out nearly £1BILLION more.

Transfermarkt figures going back to the start of the 2016/17 season show United have splashed around £1.77bn on players.



But they have brought in just £518m from sales, leaving them with a net spend of around £1.25bn and taking them to the top of the spending table.

Meanwhile, Chelsea have spent the most overall by some distance after forking out around £2.67bn on new arrivals.



That is more than £900m than United.

But the Blues have also brought in around £1.83bn from player sales, leaving them with a much lower net spend of £836m.

And when it comes to it Manchester City, Arsenal AND Tottenham all sit above Chelsea when it comes to money spent minus money received.

City are second behind United on around £1.10bn, followed by Arsenal on £1.09bn and Spurs on £942m.

Chelsea’s huge turnover is also clear from the numbers, with 83 arrivals and 125 departures compared with United’s 48 signings and 48 exits.

United’s record signing came right at the start of the period when Paul Pogba returned from Juventus for a then-world-record £89m in 2016.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The Frenchman eventually walked away for nothing six years later.

And meanwhile HUGE fees have also been spent on Anthony, Harry Maguire, Romelu Lukaku, and Jadon Sancho.

City smashed their own transfer record this summer by signing Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea for £125m on deadline day.

That matched the British transfer record and came only weeks after they splashed another £116m on Elliot Anderson.



Chelsea also broke their club record in July by paying Aston Villa £117m for Morgan Rogers, knocking £115m Moises Caicedo off top spot.

But Fernandez going the other way for £125m helps show exactly why their net figure is so much lower despite the amount they have spent.

Arsenal’s biggest deal remains the £105m move for Declan Rice from West Ham in 2023.



Meanwhile Liverpool broke the British record last year with their £125m move for Alexander Isak.

They nearly matched it again this summer by landing Bradley Barcola from PSG for an initial £107m, while Tottenham also joined the £100m club with Sandro Tonali.

Outside England, PSG sit fourth for total spending over the period and still hold the world record after paying Barcelona £200m for Neymar in 2017.



Barcelona are ninth despite their huge £142m move for Philippe Coutinho, while Real Madrid are only 14th after breaking their club record this summer for £115m Yan Diomande.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Bayern Munich do not even make the top 15, while Newcastle complete the Premier League’s presence in the top ten after cashing in on huge sales for Isak and Tonali in recent years.

And the spending is showing no signs of slowing down, with Prem clubs splashing a record £3.46bn during this summer’s window alone.

Sports.title: LaLiga star breaks down in floods of tears as he leaves Betis after 14 YEARS to help them avoid financial punishment
Sports.content:
PABLO GARCIA was in floods of tears after leaving boyhood club Real Betis on deadline day.

The 20-year-old joined Racing Santander despite featuring in all three of Betis‘ LaLiga games so far this term.



Garcia, who joined his hometown club at the age of six, even scored a late winner at Valencia last week.

Amid LaLiga’s strict financial rules, however, Betis made the difficult decision to sell the academy product to Racing Santander.



In a video circulating on social media, Garcia can be seen driving away from Betis for a final time alongside his mother.

Both can be seen in floods of tears during the heart-wrenching video as Garcia waved goodbye to gathered fans.

The left winger’s exit enabled Betis to bring back his fellow academy graduate Dani Ceballos while complying with LaLiga financial rules.

Former Arsenal midfielder Ceballos, 30, returns following nine years at Real Madrid, during which he spent two seasons on loan with the Gunners.

Many fans expressed their frustration with the situation on social media.

Sports.title: Arsenal, Man Utd and Liverpool facing new deadline after late summer transfers completed
Sports.content:
Arsenal, Man Utd and Liverpool facing new deadline after late summer transfers completed

Transfer deadline day saw several late deals done across the Premier League - and nine clubs across the top flight now face another deadline just 48 hours later

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta's Arsenal are one of eight Premier League clubs who must register squads with UEFA (Image: Getty Images)

The nine Premier League clubs competing in UEFA competitions this season have until 11pm tonight (Wednesday, September 2) to register their squads for the relevant league phases.

‌



That includes Arsenal, Aston Villa, Liverpool, Manchester City and Manchester United in the Champions League, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace and Sunderland in the Europa League and Brighton & Hove Albion in the Conference League.

‌



All nine teams can include up to 25 players on their list, while at least two of them that they name must be goalkeepers.

‌



A minimum of eight must also be 'locally trained players'. At most, half of that octet can be 'association-trained players'.

As such, at least four must be 'club-trained players'. UEFA defines them as players who were registered with the club for three entire seasons or 36 months between the ages of 15 and 21.

Enzo Fernandez reveals Chelsea truth in emotional statement on Man City transfer READ MORE :

'Association-trained players' are those who have been registered at one or multiple clubs from the same association between those same ages and for the same time period. Not registering at least eight 'locally trained players' reduces the maximum number of players a club can then register.

‌



Villa also face further restrictions. UEFA fined them £19million for a significant breach of their squad cost rule in 2025.

They are not permitted to register any new players unless their list balance is positive. For the balance to be positive, their new signing costs must be lower than their savings from player sales.

View 2 Images Manchester City face another deadline to register Enzo Fernandez for the Champions League (Image: PA Wire)

‌

Sports.title: How Man Utd managed to end up without a new left-back despite late call to rivals
Sports.content:
How Man Utd managed to end up without a new left-back despite late call to rivals

Manchester United were able to secure several midfield signings over the summer but missed out on adding a left-back despite identifying several targets and making a late call to their rivals

View 2 Images Luke Shaw remains Man Utd's left-back after the club failed to get any signings through the door

Manchester United were able to address their immediate priority this summer, which was bolstering their midfield, but ultimately missed out on adding a left-back, which was also on their agenda.

‌



The Red Devils ploughed more than £150million into their midfield with Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba all moving to Old Trafford.

‌



But despite being linked with a host of names in recent months Michael Carrick was unable to improve his backline. Seeking more cover at left-back was on their radar this summer with the reliance on Luke Shaw becoming a concern.

‌



The Englishman showed himself to be more durable last season, playing in every game, but in the years before that the former Southampton man has spent long periods out injured. He's also now into his 30s and was exposed for Ipswich's opening goal on Sunday - owning the mistake himself post-match.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

United's backline hasn't had a notable signing in two years. It is seen as the next area the club will strengthen, but that will likely have to wait until next summer. Until then Carrick could come to bemoan the failure to add more quality - not that United can be accused of failing to identify potential targets.

‌



Four players missed

Lewis Hall was the most high profile left-back that the Manchester outfit were linked with. He's just enjoyed the best year of his career to date with Newcastle, but after the Magpies cashed in on a host of their leading lights, they were determined not to sell another of their top performers. Even if Newcastle had been prepared to sell, the likelihood is that United would've lacked the finances to pursue the deal.

Barcelona's Alejandro Balde is someone who was on the market. A loan deal could've been pursued and, despite a deadline day check in on the player, United opted against trying to land the Spaniard.

View 2 Images Rayan Ait-Nouri emerged as a late target for Man Utd (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

‌



Jorge Sanilas at Racing Santander is highly-rated in La Liga and was reported to have a relatively modest release clause. Atletico Madrid were heavily linked with him, as were Barcelona, and ultimately United never backed up their interest with a bid.

It meant Carrick's options beyond Shaw, who will need to prove he can rediscover his top form, are teenager Harry Amass. The 19-year-old was tipped for a loan move to the Championship, but ultimately remained at the Championship. Diogo Dalot is among those who could swap from the right to the left if needed.

As United desperately sought solutions they put in a late call to Manchester City. Deals between the two have been few and far between but that didn't stop them making a shock approach for Rayan Ait-Nouri.

‌



The Manchester Evening News have confirmed that they approached to see whether Ait-Nouri would be available. But City were only prepared consider a loan with an obligation to make the move permanent - the Red Devils didn't want to commit to signing Ait-Nouri permanently, and thus a deal for the Algeria international failed to materialise.

All of which has left United right where they started.

Sports.title: All 20 Premier League club's biggest problems despite record-breaking transfer window
Sports.content:
The summer of all summer splurges is finally done with the conclusion of the transfer window last night.

Premier League clubs have once again spent astronomical sums of money in a bid to improve their squads, Some have managed it. Others have struggled. But all have contributed to yet another record outlay, with spending surpassing the previous £3.14bn record which was set last year.

Manchester City were the biggest contributors on deadline day, spending £125m on Enzo Fernandez and a further £65m on Iliman Ndiaye.

They are among those who've invested heavily in a bid to try and catch Arsenal, who are heavily tipped to retain their Premier League crown. Liverpool and Manchester United have secured some notable deals, the Reds spending £123m on Bradley Barcola.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Arsenal themselves have added plenty of quality - but no squad is perfect. We take a look at where each team could still be slightly short despite a record spend by England's top flight.

Arsenal

In fairness to Arsenal, it's easier said than done upgrading a squad which came within a whisker of a Premier League and Champions League double. But at the same time, it feels like a massive opportunity missed given it was obvious where Arsenal needed to level up.

‌



With mega-money deals for Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior failing to materialise, though, Arsenal are starting the season with Christos Tzolis as their first choice left attacker. Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard are also no longer on the books, so there's an argument that Arsenal are even starting the season with a weaker attack than the one that won them the title. Not exactly ideal.

View 11 Images Bruno Guimaraes was Arsenal's headline signing of the summer (Image: Offside via Getty Images)

Aston Villa

Leadership and experience is what Villa are missing following a drastic summer of change which saw the core of their Europa League-winning side depart. Emi Martinez, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans, Morgan Rogers and Ollie Watkins were the heart and soul of Unai Emery’s side last season.

‌



Villa have tried to replace them, but in many cases they’ve gone for potential over proven ability. The likes of John McGinn and Victor Lindelof will have a huge job on their hands this season as the new-look squad tries to gel on and off the pitch.

Bournemouth

Barring the change of manager, with Marco Rose replacing Andoni Iraola, it’s been a relatively quiet summer for Bournemouth, who haven’t followed the trend from previous years by selling a clutch of stars. Alex Scott remains a Cherry and that’s a major boost.

Junior Kroupi’s foot injury may have saved him from serious transfer interest, but it has left Bournemouth a touch short up front, where Evanilson doesn’t have much back-up. Alvaro Rodriguez will likely take time to settle following his move from Elche, while Daniel Jebbison has a lot to prove at this level after consecutive Championship loan spells.

‌



View 11 Images Keeping hold of Alex Scott could prove to be the best bit of business at Bournemouth (Image: James Gill/Danehouse)

Brentford

To their credit the Bees have enjoyed a sensational window. The club who always seem to have a plan and act in a smart way. They may well have landed the best value signing of the summer after landing Mamadou Sangare from Lens for £39m. Their performances to begin the season have impressed and beyond the fear of injuries to key individuals like Igor Thiago or Mikkel Damsgaard there's little room for concern.

Brighton

‌



The obvious concern will be whether the Carlos Baleba hole can be suitably filled. The Cameroonian moved to Manchester United, albeit after a year where his level did dip. Nevertheless he was a major presence in the middle of the pitch. In an effort to plug that gap Chema Andes was signed on deadline day, but much will obviously rest on how quickly he can adapt.

Danny Welbeck is back at one of the country's power clubs in Chelsea. His departure could be telling given the influence he had in the final third, even if Brighton have started the season with seven goals in two games.

Chelsea

In fairness to Chelsea, there was one area of their squad which was in obvious need of a serious upgrade. But with Emi Martinez now in the door at Stamford Bridge, it's harder to nail down an obvious area of weakness in a pretty stacked squad.

‌



View 11 Images Xabi Alonso failed to get in a replacement for Enzo Fernandez (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

After sanctioning the departure of Fernandez for a British record equalling transfer fee, it was surprising to see no replacement arrive. After all, the Argentine had spent the summer flirting with Real Madrid and then Man City; it wasn't like his exit came out of left-field. Chelsea have some serious firepower including a front three who could be the most deadly in the Premier League. But central midfield looks noticeably less star-studded than other areas of Chelsea's squad.

Coventry

The Sky Blues have invested heavily following promotion, but I can’t see where the goals are going to come from. Ellis Simms strikes me as a classic case of a player who is decent in the Championship but out of place in the Premier League, while Haji Wright is also unproven at the top level.

‌



The arrival of Taiwo Awoniyi is a good one – and suits Frank Lampard’s crossing heavy style of play – but the Nigerian has 21 goals in 92 Premier League appearances and isn’t going to fire them to safety. Jack Rudoni, Ephron Mason-Clark and Brandon Thomas-Asante are going to need to chip in after Coventry drew a blank in their opening two games.

Crystal Palace

Palace have lost Marc Guehi and Maxence Lacroix – their best two centre-backs – in successive windows for a combined £72m and haven’t replaced them like-for-like. Takehiro Tomiyasu has arrived on a free transfer, while Axel Disasi and Honest Ahanor have joined on loan. That has left Palace open to accusations of trying to do things on the cheap.

View 11 Images Maxence Lacroix swapped Crystal Palace for Chelsea (Image: John Walton/PA Wire)

‌



Pierre Sage was always going to have a difficult job after Oliver Glasner’s exit, but the lack of experienced defenders is going to make it even harder, especially after Daniel Munoz was lost to Nottingham Forest.

Everton

The hole left by Iliman Ndiaye, who moved to Manchester City, is one that will be hard to fill, at least until January. They did manage to land Jack Grealish once again, but last term the two were able to play in tandem, when Grealish was fit. Now more will be placed upon Everton's players in the final third.

Rebuilding bridges may also be among the biggest issue post-the transfer window. Everton did eventually call off a proposed deal to sell midfielder Harrison Armstrong to Nottingham Forest, but only after serious backlash from the club's supporters.

‌



A bid of £40m plus a potential sell-on clause for the England Under-19 international could've seen him leave Merseyside, which would've been tough to stomach given Armstrong is seen as one of the brightest prospects to emerge from Finch Farm in recent years. Everton supporters said there would be a "riot" if he was sold. The board, led by chair Dan Friedkin, eventually decided to reject Forest's bid.

View 11 Images Iliman Ndiaye was a key figure in the final third for Everton, but left for Man City (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

Fulham

Fulham failed to have a shot on target in their 1-0 defeat by Sunderland on the weekend and it’s hardly surprising when you look at their attacking options. The Cottagers have allowed Alvaro Arbeloa a lot of sway on their summer deals, with Real Madrid youngsters Gonzalo Garcia and César Palacios the two major arrivals. They are 22 and 21 respectively and barely have any first-team experience, let alone Premier League experience.

‌



Raul Jimenez is gone, Rodrigo Muniz blows hot and cold and there is very little other firepower in the squad, with wingers Kevin and Oscar Bobb yet to prove their worth in a Fulham shirt.

Ipswich

The Tractor Boys are going to concede an awful lot of goals this season. Manchester United looked toothless against Hull on the opening weekend and then banged in five (which could’ve been many more) against Gary O’Neil’s side.

Jacob Greaves was part of the Ipswich squad which was relegated in 2024/25 and looked some way short of Premier League quality against United. Ipswich have signed Premier League experience in the form of Issa Diop, but Dara O’Shea at right-back doesn’t look like a viable option. New goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen is going to be a busy man, with O’Neil unlikely to opt for a defence-first tactical approach.

‌



View 11 Images The Ipswich defence leaked goals last time out

Hull

The season couldn't have started better for the Tigers, who have a 100 percent record so far, but they'll no doubt be up against it at points this season. They finished sixth, some 22 points off champions Coventry, but still won promotion via the play-offs last term so the obvious concern will be the overall quality of their squad given they now have to mix it with the Premier League's elite. Nobel Mendy has arrived for a record fee and immediate shown his class, an injury to him could be something Hull struggle to cope with.

Leeds

‌



The Yorkshire side secured a point on Sunday courtesy of Dominic Calvert-Lewin's late strike, but the dependence on the former Everton striker remains. He excelled last season, scoring 15 times, but the lack of cover beyond him is notable.

He has dovetailed well in the final third with the likes Lukas Nmecha, who assisted his goal last time out, but an injury to either of those would leave Leeds short. Daniel Farke will feel more comfortable with his defence, owing to the major captures of James Trafford and Tarik Muharemovic, but goals win games and last term Calvert-Lewin and Nmecha were responsible for 40 percent of Leeds' goals.

View 11 Images The balance of Liverpool's midfield remains a concern

Liverpool

‌



The fact it’s hard to choose one position tells you a lot about Liverpool’s transfer window. But I would say that keeping Cody Gakpo is wise and at least means it’s not just Rio Ngumoha on the right wing.

Jamie Carragher had been desperate for a new central midfielder, which undoubtedly would’ve been advantageous. But I think right-back is even more precarious, with Jeremie Frimpong essentially unchallenged as the first-choice in the position, with Conor Bradley a long-term injury absentee. Frimpong is rapid, but isn’t a great defender and his crossing in the first two games of the season have shown just how good Trent Alexander-Arnold really was.

Manchester City

It's definitely a new-look Manchester City who will be vying for another Premier League title under Enzo Maresca. But have they really replaced the best defensive midfielder in the land after agreeing to sell Rodri to Barcelona?

‌



View 11 Images Enzo Maresca is taked with continuing the success of the Pep Guardiola era

They have spent the best part of £300m to 'upgrade' their engine room with mega-bucks deals for Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Ayyoub Bouaddi. Who could all be sensational signings. But there is still a Rodri-shaped hole in that Man City midfield.

Manchester United

United seem prepared to heavily target one area per summer at the moment, 12 months after they invested heavily in the attack they ploughed over £150m into their midfield. That has left the defence exposed though.

‌



No major recruit for the backline has been added in two years and United can be got at in that area. They've conceded twice in each of their opening two games and the lack of a world class individuals, especially when compared to their rivals, is obvious. The lack of depth is also clear, an injury to Luke Shaw, or a centre-half could leave Michael Carrick's side exposed at the back.

Newcastle

Newcastle have taken some heavy hits in recent windows and losing Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes would not have been part of their big summer plan. But the Magpies have regrouped and done plenty of positive business.

View 11 Images Matias Fernandez Pardo was a deadline day signing at St James' Park (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Do they have the teeth in attack to ensure they enjoy a better campaign under Matthias Jaissle? It's been a fine start and already both Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa look far more dangerous than they did last year. Newcastle added the versatile Matias Fernandez-Pardo to their ranks from Lille on deadline day with Nick Woltemade heading out on loan to Juventus. Guimaraes was Newcastle's top scorer last with nine goals with Woltemade one behind. It feels like they are short of an out and out No 9 to score the goals needed to get back into the Champions League picture.

Nottingham Forest

Central midfield appears a bit thin to me, which is hardly surprising after the departure of star man Elliot Anderson. James McAtee caught the eye at Anfield on the weekend but lacks the tenacity and ball-winning ability to play in Oliver Glasner’s demanding two-man midfield. Xaver Schlager arrived on a free transfer from Leipzig, and the Austrian knows Glasner well having worked under him at Wolfsburg, but has huge boots to fill.

Sunderland

‌



The £25.7m deadline day deal for Malick Fofana addressed an issue on the wing, but doubt remains over whether the Black Cats have enough depth on their squad to cope with Premier League and Europa League campaigns. The difficulty of playing two games per week and the travel that comes with it will tell.

Sunderland’s best starting XI is largely unchanged from last season’s impressive campaign, but Regis Le Bris will have to rely on the back-up players at times. If Granit Xhaka, Dom Ballard or Enzo Le Fee are unavailable, will their replacement step up to the mark? A gruelling season awaits.

View 11 Images Sandro Tonali is the most expensive of Tottenham's summer signings (Image: Getty Images)

Tottenham

‌



Spurs have splashed a serious amount of cash in an attempt to improve on back-to-back 17th-place finishes and they surely will do just that. But there are a few obvious weaknesses. One is at right-back, where Pedro Porro is the only specialist, leaving Archie Gray as an awkward back-up.

But the most glaring issue might be up front, where Dominic Solanke hasn’t impressed. Richarlison was keen to leave for Everton on deadline day. And while a fine addition, Omar Marmoush isn’t a centre-forward and will have a lot of expectation on his shoulders.

Sports.title: Enzo Fernandez completes record Man City transfer continuing Premier League trend
Sports.content:
Enzo Fernandez completes record Man City transfer continuing Premier League trend

Manchester City have pulled off by far the biggest deal of transfer deadline day, signing Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea for £125million to reunite him with Enzo Maresca

View 3 Images (Image: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

Manchester City have waited until the last minute to complete the deal that everyone saw coming. Enzo Fernandez has officially left Chelsea to be reunited with Enzo Maresca in Manchester.

‌



City have agreed to pay a £125million transfer fee, which makes Fernandez the joint-most expensive player in Premier League history, alongside Alexander Isak, who left Newcastle for Liverpool last summer. Fernandez is no stranger to a record fee, having only joined Chelsea from Benfica in 2023 for £107m, which was then a British record.

‌



Fernandez's exit from Stamford Bridge has long been expected. He was dropped for two games by Liam Rosenior in April after openly flirting with Real Madrid during the international break and was booed by a section of the home crowd last month, following his involvement in Argentina's controversial World Cup campaign.

‌



Despite his contentious nature, Fernandez retains a strong relationship with Maresca, who left Chelsea under a cloud on New Year's Day. Maresca has pushed for his arrival at City following the departures of four midfielders.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Rodri, Tijjani Reijnders, Nico Gonzalez and Bernardo Silva have all left City for pastures new this summer, leaving an obvious void that needed to be filled, despite Elliot Anderson's £116m arrival from Nottingham Forest and Ayoub Bouaddi joining from Lille for £86m.

The hefty transfer fee sees Fernandez top the list of massive transfers this summer, ahead of Bradley Barcola (£123m from Paris Saint-Germain to Liverpool), Morgan Rogers (£117m from Aston Villa to Chelsea) and Anderson (£116m from Nottingham Forest to City).

His move also means that seven of the top 10 deals this summer have involved Premier League sides selling to one another. That reflects the fact that the Premier League is further pulling away from the other top European leagues in terms of financial weight.

‌



View 3 Images Enzo Fernandez will form a midfield partnership with Elliot Anderson worth £241m (Image: Michael Steele/Getty Images)

In the age of profit and sustainability rules (PSR), we are also seeing a shift from clubs refusing to sell to rivals to certain clubs develop trading relationships with each other.

'Mind-blowing deal'

Analysis by John Cross

‌



The Enzo Fernandez deal feels mind-blowing because he has hardly set the world alight with his performances for Chelsea since his £106m move in January 2023. But Chelsea stand to make a tidy profit from the £125m record fee from Manchester City.

Fernandez also helped them win a European trophy, get back in the Champions League and lift the Club World Cup.

He played his best football under Enzo Maresca so that link-up will be key for his performances at City. And at the heart of this deal is that relationship. Fernandez had his heart set on playing for Maresca again which is a feather in the cap for the new City boss.

‌



View 3 Images Enzo Maresca will be reunited with Enzo Fernandez at Manchester City (Image: Chris Lee - Chelsea FC/Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

There was serious interest from other clubs this summer because, while he may not always get huge appreciation in the Premier League, he is a World Cup winner with a remarkable mentality.

Fernandez will have to use that mental strength to overcome some of the barracking after the last World Cup and also the spotlight that a huge fee brings.

‌



He flirted with Real Madrid last season which was quickly killed by the Spanish giants. But as soon as City showed interest this summer, he had his heart set on that switch.

The contract is expected to take him until 2032 in whatever form but the personal terms were clearly never going to be an issue.

Sports.title: Man Utd issue instant response as Everton make deadline day bid for striker
Sports.content:
Man Utd issue instant response as Everton make deadline day bid for striker

Everton are understood to have made a last-minute bid to sign Manchester United striker Joshua Zirkzee before the summer transfer window closes

View 2 Images Joshua Zirkzee of Manchester United (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Joshua Zirkzee will be remaining at Manchester United this summer, despite a deadline day approach from Everton. Zirkzee has been heavily linked with a move away from Old Trafford throughout the summer, with the Netherlands international facing an uncertain future.

‌



Fiorentina and Juventus have previously been mentioned as potential destinations for Zirkzee this summer, although no deal was able to be agreed with either of the Serie A duo, which would have seen the striker return to Italy.

‌



Zirkzee could now remain in the Premier League with the latest updates suggesting that a move to Merseyside could have been on the cards.

‌



Everton are understood to have submitted a proposal to United in a bid to bring Zirkzee to Goodison Park on a loan basis, as they seek to bolster their attacking options.

Man Utd suffer late transfer deadline day blow as Man City reject approach for star READ MORE :

Man Utd in talks to sign ANOTHER midfielder before the transfer deadline READ MORE :

The Toffees have also been strongly linked with Monaco striker Folarin Balogun in recent days, though reports suggest that particular deal could be in doubt ahead of the deadline.

Consequently, it is believed that Everton had identified Zirkzee as an alternative to Balogun, should a transfer for the former Arsenal centre forward fail to materialise.

‌



However, it's understood that Zirkzee will remain at United beyond the 11pm deadline and until the January transfer, at the very least.

It was understood that Zirkzee would welcome a switch to Everton, though such a move would have left United with little time to bring in a replacement.

‌



Zirkzee has found himself slipping down the pecking order at Old Trafford over the past year, particularly following United's busy transfer activity last summer.

The arrivals of Bryan Mbeumo, Benjamin Sesko and Matheus Cunha at United last year left Zirkzee with little time on the pitch during the previous campaign, fuelling speculation that he could be heading for the exit door this summer.

Zirkzee is yet to feature for United this season, having been named as an unused substitute in both of their opening Premier League fixtures against Hull City and Ipswich Town.

‌



Carrick was quizzed on the prospect of United bringing in further reinforcements following their 5-2 victory over Ipswich at the weekend.

View 2 Images Joshua Zirkzee of Manchester United (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

"It's always difficult to say, to be honest, when there's so little time left," Carrick said.

"I think the situation that we're in, I think the business that we've managed to do, I'm pleased with. I think we're a better group, a better squad, potentially a better team.

"Adding Marcus [Rashford] into that feels like a new signing. So, in that respect, we're quite happy.

Article continues below

"We're always open to if there's something else to be able to add, so I wouldn't shut that down, but as it stands, we'll have to wait and see."

Sports.title: Man Utd suffer transfer deadline day blow as Man City respond to shock approach for star
Sports.content:
Man Utd suffer transfer deadline day blow as Man City respond to shock approach for star

Manchester United were in the market for another left-back in the final hours of the transfer window but a potential deal for Rayan Ait-Nouri did not materialise

View Image Rayan Ait-Nouri was offered to Manchester United prior to transfer deadline day (Image: Vince Mignott/MB Media)

Manchester United's search for a new left-back on deadline day led to them making a shock approach for Rayan Ait-Nouri, it has emerged.

‌



The Red Devils have been active in the summer transfer window, bringing three new central midfielders to the club in Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba. But they have been frustrated in their attempts to sign a new left-back to compete with first-choice Luke Shaw.

‌



As speculation over United's plans grew on deadline day, The Manchester Evening News have confirmed that they approached their bitter rivals Manchester City to gauge whether Ait-Nouri would be available after being offered the defender by his agent.

‌



City would only consider a loan with an obligation to make the move permanent for a player who only moved to The Etihad last summer.

But with United not interested in committing to signing Ait-Nouri permanently, a deal for the Algeria international failed to materialise.

‌



Signed for £36m from Wolves, Ait-Nouri has found himself behind Nico O'Reilly and Josko Gvardiol in the City pecking order, with the latter starting the season at left-back for Manchester City.

Shaw is Manchester United's only senior recognised left-back with Patrick Dorgu now seen as an option further forward on the wing.

Their search for reinforcements has seen them make enquiries for the Barcelona left-back, Alejandro Balde, in recent days, but again United were only interested in a loan deal for the 22-year-old.

United also considered a late swoop for Racing Santander's Jorge Salinas before deciding against pursuing a deal.

Sports.title: Gabriel Jesus makes honest Julian Alvarez admission after leaving Arsenal for Barcelona
Sports.content:
Gabriel Jesus makes honest Julian Alvarez admission after leaving Arsenal for Barcelona

Gabriel Jesus has signed a three-year contract with Barcelona, where he's become their alternative to Julian Alvarez, after leaving Arsenal in a deal worth £12.85million

View 2 Images Gabriel Jesus spoke honestly at his unveiling by Barcelona (Image: Javier Borrego/Europa Press via Getty Images)

Gabriel Jesus has admitted he isn't bothered about being Barcelona's second choice after Julian Alvarez following his transfer from Arsenal.

‌



Jesus has signed a three-year contract with Barca, who agreed to pay the Gunners a fee which could reach £12.85million. The Brazilian entered the final year of his deal in north London and Mikel Arteta made it clear that he didn't feature in his plans for the 2026/27 season.

‌



He was frozen out of the first-team set-up along with Gabriel Martinelli and has now landed on his feet in Barcelona. The Catalan giants had wanted to sign Alvarez instead, but Atletico Madrid released a statement to publicly state they wouldn't do business with their La Liga rivals after growing irritated by their interest.

‌



Jesus rejected a move to Napoli and his decision ended up paying dividends, with a dream transfer to Barca the result. "A week ago I received a message that it could happen," he said at his unveiling. "When I started to think it was a real possibility, I was so excited. Now I can't wait to start training and playing.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Chelsea have Arsenal and Tottenham players on five-man Enzo Fernandez replacement list READ MORE :

"It doesn't annoy me [being Plan B to Alvarez], it doesn't bother me. What annoys me is if people say I'm a bad guy, which has never happened in my life - or if I am not playing football, that bothers me.

‌



"I have the chance to play for Barcelona, a chance I had 10 years ago and now life has offered me that opportunity again."

Jesus joined Arsenal from Manchester City in 2022 for £45million, but his time in Arteta's side never really worked out. He slipped behind Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres in the pecking order and leaves having scored 32 goals in 123 appearances for the Gunners.

View 2 Images Julian Alvarez looks set to stay at Atletico Madrid (Image: Angel Martinez, Getty Images)

‌



"I took a significant salary drop, but it's a dream to be here," Jesus added. "But it wasn't just me who had to make an effort to get the transfer over line, Barca also played their part.

"If you had asked me one month ago, I would have said it was unlikely this would happen. At 29, I didn't think I would have the chance to come to Barca."

He made 27 appearances in all competitions for Arsenal last season after recovering from a cruciate ligament knee injury. But after a summer of training he feels ready to hit the ground running for Hansi Flick's side, who needed a replacement for Robert Lewandowski.

Article continues below

"The last two years have been really complicated after the knee injury," Jesus said. "I was out of the game for almost one year, but it's in the past. I feel good physically now. I recovered well, returned to action for Arsenal and I am 100 per cent ready to play and give my all."

Sports.title: Etienne chases first success at Bath
Sports.content:
We have a busy day’s racing on Wednesday with flat action from Bath and Newcastle, live on Sky Sports Racing...

2.00 Bath - Promising Etienne returns following Super Sprint fourth

Promising Etienne returns following Super Sprint fourth in the EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes.

Richard Spencer-trained Etienne was touched off by a short head on debut before improving further when finishing fourth in the Weatherbys Super Sprint.

He shaped best that day, conceding first run and running on to finish with the highest finishing speed of the front four.

The winner, Angel's Lane has since bolted up to win a good edition of the St Hugh's Stakes, and the level of form that Etienne brings to the race, looks a class apart from his rivals.

He contains Group One and Group Two entries this autumn, and the slight step up in trip should see him to best effect, and extremely tough to beat.

Tree Wizard and Anna Belardo contain one piece of form each which could see them run creditably against Etienne, but both need to bounce back to their best if they're to threaten Richard Spencer's runner.

5.02 Bath - Quebella headlines trappy fillies' handicap

Quebella headlines a trappy contest in the British EBF Fillies' Handicap.

Quebella has strung together two creditable third-placed finishes since moving to Owen Burrows.

She was very well backed last time out at Chester but a wide trip and drop in trip both did not see her to best effect. Back up a furlong and a half should suit, and she should go well.

Pierian looked promising when winning by nine lengths at Yarmouth in May, but has since disappointed. She was put into listed company before a handicap at Glorious Goodwood, so she is definitely thought better of, and she can prove competitive if progressing from her earlier season efforts.

The in-form duo, Mythical Bird and Aravalli both scored last time out, with the latter succeeding in four of her last five starts.

They should both go well in a wide-open fillies' handicap.

2.45 Newcastle - Intriguing 3yo Yordan bids to back up facile success

Intriguing three-yearold Yordan bids to back up facile success in the EBF Novice Stakes.

Yordan was purchased for 160,000gns as a yearling in October 2024, but had to wait until July 2026 to make his belated debut. He has made a promising start at three, finishing a close second on debut, before winning by nearly three lengths, going away when dropped to six furlongs last month at Southwell.

Harry Vigors has been booked to ride which offsets the winning penalty he shoulders, and with a clear class edge on paper, he could take all the beating when attempting to make it two wins from three.

Ennoble was previously trained by Joseph O'Brien and contains solid two-year-old form. However, Antony Brittain would need to revitalise this horse as it seems like he may not have trained on.

Brash has held a consistent level of form to date and can again run creditably; however, he is much more exposed and would need to make a miraculous improvement to even threaten Yordan.

Best of the rest

4.30 Bath - Course specialist, Blue Hero aims for 12th course win vs in-form Buckland Belle.

4.45 Newcastle - Let's Go Hugo bids for a hat-trick.

Eight-race Lyon-Parilly and Toulouse cards.

Sports.title: 'Fans will crucify them' - Hakkinen issues warning over team orders in title battle
Sports.content:
Two-time world champion Mika Hakkinen has warned that Formula 1 teams risk 'being crucified' by the sport's fans if they implement team orders in an attempt to influence this year's title battle.

Kimi Antonelli leads his Mercedes team-mate George Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton by 59 points at the top of the standings, with McLaren's Lando Norris 83 points back in fourth after belatedly igniting his title defence with victories at the last two races.

With 11 rounds remaining, Hamilton is 28 points clear of his Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc, while Norris has moved 55 points ahead of his McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri.

Given the significant margins by which the British duo each trail Antonelli, it has been a topic of speculation as to whether either Ferrari or McLaren would consider implementing team orders sooner rather than later to aid their better-positioned driver in the title fight.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix

Hakkinen, who spoke to Sky Sports News in his role as a Laureus Academy Member, said: "Which team is going to do this kind of change and what are the arguments they are going to give and tell the fans? This is going to be an important factor.

"All these drivers have a huge fanbase these days in the world, and if the team are going to decide one day that this driver is going to be number two, the fans are going to crucify this team.

"So, you have to be very careful these days how you are activating these kinds of team orders."

Image: Two-time F1 world champion Mika Hakkinen believes team orders could be a crucial factor in the title battle

'Hamilton's Dutch GP emotion absolutely normal'

The issue of team orders became a talking point at the Dutch Grand Prix when Hamilton became infuriated with his Ferrari team after he was held by Leclerc.

After the race, Hamilton pointed out the contrast between the approaches of Ferrari and Mercedes, who were decisive in ordering Russell to let Antonelli past him having adjusted the Italian's strategy to fend off the threat coming from the seven-time world champion.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton outlined his frustrations after a fourth-place finish at the Dutch Grand Prix

Hamilton later posted on social media expressing regret for the tone of his comments to the media and over the radio during the Zandvoort race, but Hakkinen says his reaction was "absolutely normal".

"I think what Lewis experienced in Zandvoort, it was explained from the team why it happened," Hakkinen said.

"Emotions with Lewis' experience was absolutely normal. Maybe it wasn't only emotion, just also common sense. 'We can score more points if you let me overtake!'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on The Fast And The Curious podcast, Betty Glover, Christian Hewgill and Greg James reflect on their favourite radio messages from the Dutch GP

"But nowadays when I look at Grand Prix racing from the outside, when I'm in the paddock, it's different. You see much more, you get much more information on what's happening.

"The drivers are getting only a very tiny percentage of the information we get on TV, so when they are following another car and it doesn't let them overtake, they don't have the information and the calculations that the team have, so then very often you get these kind of reactions from the drivers, which is very normal."

'Schumacher would get team orders in first race of season'

Hakkinen reflected on his own experience of team orders during title races, with the Finnish driver having come up against Michael Schumacher when the seven-time world champion had clear number-one status at Ferrari.

Hakkinen won successive drivers' titles in 1998 and 1999 before finishing second to Schumacher in 2000 as the German won the first of five successive championships at Ferrari.

"The fanbase has changed in Formula 1; the generation is different than in my time," Hakkinen said.

"When I was racing against Michael Schumacher when he was at Ferrari, they started doing team orders already at the first race of the season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ferrari has unveiled its one-off livery, paying tribute to Michael Schumacher, for the Formula 1 Italian Grand Prix at Monza

"It was very obvious that if one driver is very strong in a team and started to win races and score points, the team is very much aware that if they want to win the world championship, they need to support this one driver 100 per cent.

"That's what Michael Schumacher was able to manage to do with Ferrari when he was racing there.

"We had a little bit of a different philosophy at McLaren. We wanted to give both drivers the same opportunity until the points were at a point that one couldn't catch the other; then the team-mate has to start supporting the leading driver. That was a common-sense operation.

"Now the teams want to win the Drivers' Championship and the Constructors' Championship, they want to win both. So. it's important that both drivers are getting maximum performance all the time in every race."

Hakkinen was speaking to Sky Sports in his role as a Laureus Academy Member ahead of the Spanish Grand Prix at Madring from September 11-13. Madrid, a global city of sport, is becoming the new home of the Spanish GP, after hosting the Laureus World Sports Awards in April.

Sports.title: 'I know what I have to work on' - Fery ready to take on best despite US Open exit
Sports.content:
Britain's Arthur Fery said he now knows what he has to work on after his US Open debut was cut short on Tuesday.

His hopes of making a splash in New York were ended in the first round after a straight-sets defeat by Lorenzo Musetti.

The 24-year-old had been riding the crest of a wave since his historic run to the Wimbledon semi-finals as a wildcard earlier this summer.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fery hit this tweener in a superb rally against Musetti

He reached his first ATP final at the Winston-Salem Open last week and arrived at Flushing Meadows with high hopes of another deep run at the Grand Slam.

But he ran aground against Italian 13th seed Musetti in a straight-sets loss on Grandstand Stadium.

It was a comprehensive defeat, but a useful gauge for Fery who has risen from outside the top 200 a year ago to No 33 in the world.

"I know what I have to work on," he said. "I got a lot of ideas coming straight off the court of what I have to work on to do better.

"My serve really let me down today, which is not usually the case, but I've been struggling a little bit to find my rhythm on the serve.

"Today was particularly a struggle, but definitely playing guys at that level, it's tough and the margins are small."

Fery, now the British No 1, was close to being seeded at Flushing Meadows, meaning he would have avoided a player of Musetti's class in the early stages.

He admitted he was under-prepared due to his run in North Carolina last week, but said he would not have done things differently.

"The Grand Slams are the biggest tournaments and everyone has their eye on them." he added. "At the same time, would I sign for these past two weeks? Probably, to be honest.

"It's a lot of ranking points, it's a first ATP final, so it's good. Even though it meant that my preparation for the US Open was not great."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ryan Harrison believes more players will now know how to play against Fery since his recent success but believes being exposed could also be a blessing in disguise

Fery reflects further: If I had played my A-game I would have had a chance

Speaking to Sky Sports following the loss, Fery was still disappointed and felt it was an opportunity missed.

He also cited a lack of preparation time as a learning curve early on in his career that has taken a massive stride forward.

"It was a tough, tough match and definitely a good opponent. It was not the draw that I wanted, but I felt like I had a chance to win if I put my A-game on the court. I was a bit short today," he said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Arthur Fery 'very disappointed' after first-round US Open defeat to Lorenzo Musetti.

"I practised well yesterday and felt like I was ready for today, but obviously would have loved to have a few more practice days under my belt in these conditions with the balls and the speed of the court before playing.

"It is still one of the biggest matches of my career. In terms of the stage and the court and the player, it is not like it's something that I do every week still.

"So it was a big ask. I knew that, but I was ready for the challenge. I knew it was going to be tough, but also was ready mentally to fight and try and find solutions, whatever they were. But preparation was obviously a bit hindered.

Despite his disappointment, Fery knows that these big moments will only help moving into the future as he learns more about the big stages and starts to progress even further.

"It is still positive. I have had three tournaments in the US and lost to three great players. I made my first ATP Tour final last week.

"I feel like I can still improve, which is really the great thing.

"There are a lot of aspects of my game that I can get better in. So it is moving in the right direction.

"It is my first US Open. I am really grateful to be here, to be in this position, and already looking forward to coming back next year."

'Learning curve for Fery'

Image: Fery sees areas of his game which he wants to improve

Sky Sports Tennis' Tim Henman said Fery will take "an enormous amount" from his defeat and will gain vital experience.

The former British No 1 said: "What he lacks right now is experience at the highest level. He's 33 in the world and hasn't played a great deal of tennis outside the UK at this level.

"To come up against Musetti, who is a world-class player, has been five in the world and reached semi-finals of Grand Slams, provides clear evidence of what he needs to work on."

Asked where Fery can improve his game, Henman said: "He's got to continue to give himself opportunities to finish points at the net.

"His forehand side, in these types of [hot] conditions, he can perhaps take the ball a bit earlier and get more penetration through the court.

"He can work on that first serve to get a bit more pace, which is not easy because he's not the tallest of players, but then he's got to improve that accuracy."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ryan Harrison analysed Fery's game ahead of his US Open debut

Robson: Musetti too good for Fery

Laura Robson said: "Musetti was too good. He had that extra gear to go to with his pace off the racquet and his ability to open up the lines made such a big difference.

"Fery will be a little disappointed that he wasn't able to hang in that first set. That could have changed the course of the match.

Sports.title: Gauff makes storming start as Zverev avoids major upset
Sports.content:
Coco Gauff opened her US Open campaign with a straight-sets win over Zeynep Sonmez, while two-time women's doubles champions Serena and Venus Williams are set to face Maya Joint and Chan Hao-Ching after the draw on Tuesday.

Home favourite Gauff arrived ‌fresh from winning the Cincinnati Open and is chasing a third Grand Slam title ​after her breakthrough triumph in New York in 2023.

The American, who ​has reached the fourth round or better here ​in each of the last four years, will face either Daria Kasatkina or Paula Badosa in the second ‌round.

"I wasn't that nervous today, which was a shock," Gauff said ​on court. "When I walked back out on this court, ‌I was trying to hold back a smile."

Gauff was in control early as she took the only break of serve in the first set and wrapping up the opener in just over ​half an hour.

World No 53 Sonmez showed flashes of ⁠her talent and produced a string ⁠of impressive winners, including a blistering backhand that drew applause from the crowd on Arthur Ashe Stadium and even Gauff herself.

Sonmez, 24, ‌settled in the second set, trading breaks, and began testing the American with deep ‌groundstrokes and forays to the net.

Gauff came under pressure trailing 3-2 but fought off three break points to hold and level the set before breaking Sonmez to reassert control at 4-3.

The 22-year-old pulled away from there as Sonmez ⁠struggled to sustain the level that had briefly unsettled ​the fourth seed, leaving Gauff to close out a comfortable win.

"I know that I can raise my level if ​I need to," said Gauff. "I like to challenge my opponent to ⁠keep up that level the whole match, and if they do, I clap my hands and walk off the court with my head held high. But ⁠I was able to settle down."
