Sports.title: Balogun walks away from Everton deal
Sports.content:
Everton's move for Monaco striker Folarin Balogun has fallen through following a change of heart from the player after the deal scuppered Chelsea's chances of signing Lamine Camara.

Balogun arrived in Merseyside at lunchtime to complete the £40m Deadline Day transfer, but doubts began to emerge that the deal would be completed after an issue came up in the medical.

As a result, Monaco moved to sell midfielder Camara instead, but in another twist, Everton renegotiated Balogun's deal to force the move through.

Despite having a full agreement to sell Camara to Chelsea in place, Monaco withdrew from the deal as the 11pm transfer deadline passed, which left the Blues furious.

Chelsea also had the chance to withdraw from the £125m move to sell Enzo Fernandez to Man City, but chose not to out of good faith.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol explains why Chelsea sold Enzo Fernandez to rivals Manchester City despite the last-minute collapse of their deal to sign Lamine Camara from Monaco.

However, just after midnight on Wednesday, it was revealed that Balogun had a change of heart about moving to Everton and walked away from the deal, which only infuriated Monaco and Chelsea even more.

It also means Balogun's dramatic 2026 continues - after the American international was at the centre of the World Cup red card storm involving Donald Trump.

It leaves Everton with just one recognised senior striker until January in Thierno Barry, after Beto left for Fiorentina and Manchester United rejected a loan offer for Joshua Zirkzee.

Everton's attacking options were further diminished by the departure of Iliman Ndiaye to Manchester City, but they did sign Jack Grealish on another loan deal.

The Balogun drama in chronological order

Everton agree fee with Monaco for Folarin Balogun.

Balogun arrives in Merseyside for a medical and to complete the move's formalities.

Chelsea have multiple bids rejected by Monaco for Lamine Camara. They consider other targets.

Chelsea agree deal to sell Enzo Fernandez to Man City for £125m. Comfortable with the options in their squad if no one comes in.

Doubts emerge around Everton's deal for Balogun.

Everton make an offer to sign Joshua Zirkzee from Manchester United on loan with an option to buy.

Chelsea agree a deal with Monaco for Lamine Camara, amid doubts about the Balogun deal.

Manchester United reject Everton's loan offer for Zirkzee.

Everton grow more confident they can get Balogun over the line after renegotiating with Monaco.

Chelsea's deal to sign Camara collapses after Monaco withdraw from the deal. The Balogun deal being back on satisfied their need for a sale.

Balogun had a change of heart and walked away from the deal after a deal sheet was submitted.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Re-live all the thrills and spills from Transfer Deadline Day on Sky Sports News.

Analysis: 'Balogun saga caps chaotic summer window'

Sky Sports News' Vinny O'Connor:

"That's Everton that!

"But how have they got to a situation where they've halved a strike force that was far from prolific anyway?

"Easy to say in hindsight but allowing Beto to go to Fiorentina before a deal for Folarin Balogun was signed and sealed now looks amateur at best.

"The unsuccessful pivot to Manchester United's Joshua Zirkzee when the Balogun deal initially faltered just adds to the feeling of a chaotic and panicked end to the window.

"Add to that the sale of their most exciting talent, Iliman Ndiaye. All window, it was emphasised Everton were in a position of strength given he had three years left on his contract.

"Yet, a £65m deal was agreed, more than four times what they had paid for him two years earlier. But the fee was still not high enough to make the deal acceptable to many fans.

"Of course Ndiaye was initially off to Spurs for £60m with Richarlison coming the other way for £35m. A fee for the Brazilian that, even taking into account the esteem in which he's held by the blue half of Merseyside, appeared to be on the high side and ultimately was the first of Everton's proposed deadline day deals to fall through.

"Kenny Tete was another. Fulham weren't letting him go without knowing they definitely had a replacement - a lesson in that, perhaps.

"So, a tumultuous end to a window that has been far from easy when you consider the club's ownership mulling over Nottingham Forest's £40m offer to buy Harrison Armstrong at a time when David Moyes was talking up the need for getting players in.

"After turning down big money, the club will surely want to safeguard what is effectively an investment and show of faith in his potential whilst avoiding the risk of value decreasing as his current contract runs down.

"And Evertonians could do with some positivity. At the moment, they are hurt, embarrassed, angry, frustrated, and concerned, when the facts are that it didn't need to be like this.

"Ainsley Maitland-Niles is someone who can cover both full-back positions and possesses a versatility that's much needed in David Moyes's squad.

"And, of course, there was the expected return of Jack Grealish on loan, much needed following the departure of Ndiaye.

"Earlier in the window, there was arguably a parallel with David Moyes's first spell in charge, as Hayden Hackney,the Championship player of the year, was given the opportunity to show he can make the step up to the Premier League. His first showing against Crystal Palace was promising.

"From a top division rookie to the more established, Christian Norgaard may prove a crucial piece of business, bringing his experience to the midfield with Idrissa Gana Gueye having left at the end of his contract.

"Add to that the decision to insert an obligation to buy in the loan agreement that brought Merlin Rohl to Hill Dickinson last season, and Tyrique George rejoining on a permanent deal after last season's temporary spell are two more positives judging by their early season contributions.

"However, potentially the best move of Everton's summer was the swap deal that saw Dwight McNeil leaving for Palace and Brennan Johnson coming the other way. McNeil was in the final year of his contract.

"Unfortunately, the positives mentioned are more than overshadowed by the fact that the manager has, again, not been given the tools that will give him the best chance of delivering success.

"Last season it was the failure to bring in a right-back and a proven striker. This season he has to muddle through until at least January with Thierno Barry as his only recognised front man.

"Given the circumstances, it's difficult to see them muster a challenge for Europe, and if that is the case, it shouldn't be seen as a failure."

What next for Balogun after difficult summer?

Sky Sports' Peter Smith:

Balogun had personal ambitions to join one of Europe's biggest sides this summer.

After an in-form finish to last season and a match-winning start to the World Cup, where he was celebrated in the USA as a new hero, Balogun's star was certainly on the rise.

There was also a feeling that this was the time for Monaco to make the most profit on a player with just two years remaining on his contract. A big transfer beckoned.

But his red card and the controversy of a President Trump-encouraged lifting of the subsequent suspension shifted his narrative. It wasn't Balogun's fault he was at the centre of the storm, but he had to ride the rough waves of it.

After the tournament, offers from Europe's elite didn't materialise, despite Balogun changing agent. A transfer to Everton was not what Balogun had imagined at the start of the summer.

During his time at Monaco, Balogun has enjoyed the challenge of playing on the continent and in the Champions League. The lure of the Premier League is not as strong for the former Arsenal academy graduate as it may be for others, despite other clubs from England's top flight also having held an interest in signing him.

This latest call is of his own making, though - and he will have to take the repercussions of it. But what Balogun does now is far from certain. For the second time this summer, he has been involved in a dramatic twist in a tale.

Sports.title: 'Chelsea are really unhappy!' - Monaco pull out of selling Camara
Sports.content:
Monaco have pulled out of the deal to sell Lamine Camara to Chelsea, who feel the French club have acted in an extraordinary and deeply unprofessional way.

Camara was set to join Chelsea for £47m and sign a six-year deal pending a medical.

Just after the 11pm transfer deadline passed, news emerged that Monaco reneged on their agreement with Chelsea and informed the Blues of their decision in writing.

Monaco pulled out because they had successfully renegotiated the deal to sell Folarin Balogun to Everton, only for the striker to sensationally back out at the last minute.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Rob Dorsett explains why the collapse of the Folarin Balogun deal leaves Everton short of strikers for the season.

Monaco only wanted to sell one player, and after agreeing to sell Balogun to Everton, they pulled out of the Camara-to-Chelsea deal despite a full written club-to-club agreement with the Blues.

Monaco refused to sign a Camara deal sheet before the 11pm deadline, so there was no chance of Chelsea resurrecting a deal for the Senegal international.

The feeling at Chelsea towards Monaco now is likely to be "what goes around comes around".

Chelsea had been looking for a new midfielder with Enzo Fernandez joining Manchester City in a joint-British-record £125m deal.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ben Ransom reports that finally Enzo Fernandez has completed his £125m move from Chelsea to Man City on a five-year deal.

Chelsea had the option to pull the plug on Fernandez's move to Man City after the Camara deal collapsed, but they stuck to their word and honoured their commitment to complete the deal.

Roma's Manu Kone was also shortlisted as a potential option, while Chelsea were also looking at midfield options in the Premier League.

'Chelsea are really unhappy'

Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol:

"Enzo Fernandez is going to be a Manchester City player. Lamine Camara to Chelsea collapsing is totally separate.

"Chelsea have not been able to sign a replacement. Chelsea are really unhappy with the way Monaco behaved.

"My information is everything was done - written, agreed, signed. He was flying into London [on Wednesday].

"At the same time, Monaco have been negotiating with Everton to sell Folarin Balogun. Once they agreed a deal with Everton, they came back to Chelsea and went back on their agreement.

"Chelsea don't believe this is the way clubs should conduct business. I suppose this is one of the risks you take when you leave things so late."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Re-live all the thrills and spills from Transfer Deadline Day on Sky Sports News.

Who has left Chelsea on Deadline Day?

Chelsea goalkeeper Robert Sanchez has completed a season-long loan move to Serie A side Como.

The goalkeeper had been bumped down to Stamford Bridge following the arrival of Emi Martinez from Aston Villa.

Elsewhere, midfielder Dario Essugo has completed a season-long loan move to sister club Strasbourg. Essugo was of interest to Hull in this window.

Striker Deivid Washington has completed a permanent transfer to Strasbourg. He signed from Santos for £17.1m three years ago but made only three appearances.

Forward Dujuan Richards has also joined AFC Wimbledon on a season-long loan.

Meanwhile, Chelsea striker Shim Mheuka has arrived in Glasgow ahead of his loan move to Celtic, who are also working to finalise a deal for Chelsea left-back Landon Emenalo.

Sports.title: Sunderland complete Fofana signing after dramatic saga
Sports.content:
Sunderland have finally completed the signing of Lyon winger Malick Fofana after a dramatic Deadline Day transfer saga involving two private jets and the player changing his mind multiple times.

Sunderland agreed a deal to sign Fofana on Deadline Day morning but Crystal Palace - whose manager Pierre Sage worked with him before at Lyon - tried to hijack the deal.

With both Premier League clubs agreeing a deal with Lyon for the winger, Fofana was then sat at Lyon airport, with two private jets waiting on him to make a decision. One plane was set for Sunderland, the other was set for London.

Fofana also took one medical in Lyon on Deadline Day that both teams had access to.

But just over an hour to go until the deadline, Fofana eventually chose Sunderland with Black Cats owner Kyril Louis-Dreyfus travelling to Lyon to convince the player to join.

Fofana's move to Sunderland consists of an initial £25.7m with £5.14m in add-ons.

Arsenal were also considering a move for Fofana over the weekend but did not make a move for the player.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Re-live all the thrills and spills from Transfer Deadline Day on Sky Sports News.

How a dramatic Deadline Day panned out

10:47am: After Arsenal did not take up the chance to sign Fofana, Sunderland agreed a deal with Lyon for the winger worth up to £30m.

1:01pm: Crystal Palace try to hijack Sunderland's five-year deal for Fofana by entering in direct communication with the player in an attempt to convince him to join them.

3:18pm: Crystal Palace agree a deal with Lyon for Fofana. Sunderland begin talks with fellow Belgium winger Dodi Lukebakio on top of the Fofana deal.

3.42pm: Fofana is at Lyon airport with two private jets waiting on him to make a decision - one bound for Sunderland and another for London.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports Keith Downie explains how Lyon winger Malick Fofana had the choice of TWO private jets to the UK to seal a move to a Premier League club!!

8:24pm: Sunderland owner Kyril Louis-Dreyfus visits Lyon to try and persuade Fofana to choose Sunderland over Palace. The player effectively undergoes one medical for both teams.

9:38pm: Sunderland's attempts to sign Benfica's Lukebakio end as a decision is made for him to remain with the Portuguese club.

9:50pm: Fofana gives Sunderland the green light after changing his mind multiple times throughout the day. The price of the deal rises to £30.8m.

10:54pm: Sunderland submit a deal sheet to get the Fofana deal over the line.

12:15am: Sunderland announce the Fofana deal

Sports.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
Sports.content:
Arsenal

Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martineilli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons

Key ins: Bruno Guimarães (Newcastle, £75m), Ezri Konsa (Aston Villa, £51m), Piero Hincapié (Bayer Leverkusen, £45m), Christos Tzolis (Club Brugge, £34m)

Key outs: Leandro Trossard (Besiktas, £15.3m), Jakub Kiwior (Porto, £14.5m), Gabriel Jesus (Barcelona, £8.6m), Fábio Vieira (Hamburg, £7.7m), Christian Nørgaard (Everton, £7m), Ethan Nwaneri (Borussia Dortmund, loan)

Aston Villa

It is all change at Villa and, although a little trepidation is inevitable, a refresh was probably overdue. At the same time, Unai Emery did not want to lose so many key players and Villa’s manager has made clear there is no such thing as a transition season in his eyes. Villa have generated about £300m from the sales of nine players and brought in 10 at a cost of about £250m. Villa have lowered their wage bill and changed the profile of their squad. Zion Suzuki, Ibrahim Mbaye and Johan Manzambi, names on the lips of Villa’s rivals, are particularly exciting signings. Last summer there was concern Villa had gone stale and 12 months ago they ended up fretting on deadline day – Harvey Elliott and Jadon Sancho joined on loan – but there was no such chaos this time. Ben Fisher

Key ins: Johan Manzambi (Freiburg, £51m), Nicolas Jackson (Chelsea, £47.5m), Ibrahim Mbaye (PSG, £47m), João Gomes (Wolves, £34m), Zion Suzuki (Parma, £30m), Taylor Harwood-Bellis (Southampton, £25m), Matteo Ruggeri (Atlético Madrid, £21.4m), Leon Goretzka (Bayern Munich, free), Aaron Wan-Bissaka (West Ham, loan), Alejandro Garnacho (Chelsea, loan)

Bournemouth

Perhaps Bournemouth’s best business was keeping hold of their coveted key players, chiefly Eli Junior Kroupi, Rayan, Alex Scott and Tyler Adams. Bournemouth rejected bids from Chelsea for Scott and stayed true to their plan of resisting offers to give Marco Rose the best chance of succeeding, with the club attempting to juggle European competition and the league for the first time. The arrival of the Portugal centre-back António Silva, 22, from Benfica looks a typically smart replacement for Marcos Senesi, 29. Kroupi’s freak foot injury, which will probably keep him out until November, may have proved a blessing in disguise in terms of retaining the 20-year-old. BF

Brentford

Avoiding a repeat of last year’s upheaval was a major boost. Keith Andrew held on to his best players and made smart additions to a solid squad. Mamadou Sangaré has added quality in midfield since joining from Lens and looks the bargain of the summer. Callum Wilson has brought experience up front after signing on a free and Jaidon Anthony provides cover on the flanks after his £15m move from Burnley. El Hadji-Malick Diouf, signed from West Ham, offers potential at left-back. Jacob Steinberg

Deadline day deals to bring in the exciting Nigeria forward Femi Azeez from Millwall and the Spanish midfielder Chema Andrés from Stuttgart made it 12 signings in another summer of transition, Azeez’s arrival being announced almost 12 hours after the window shut. The departures of Jan Paul van Hecke, Carlos Baleba and Carl Rushworth brought in more than £140m as the Brighton model continues to deliver big profits, although losing last season’s top scorer, Danny Welbeck, to Chelsea for a mere £5m may be the biggest loss if the new striker Promise David cannot bring the goals. Chelsea

Xabi Alonso’s appointment as manager was the biggest signing of the summer. Chelsea have been sensible since turning to the Spaniard. Morgan Rogers has started well after joining for £117m. Maxence Lacroix adds power in defence, Marco Palestra versatility on the flanks. Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson can raise standards in the dressing room. But there was the usual revolving door. Money was made on a host of outgoings. Marc Cucurella, one of the world’s best left-backs and sold to Real Madrid, looks a bigger loss than Enzo Fernández. However a worry is that Chelsea did not replace Fernández after selling him to Manchester City for £125m, their late £47m move for Monaco’s Lamine Camara collapsing at the last. JS

Sports.title: Fernández completes record-equalling £125m move from Chelsea to Manchester City
Sports.content:
Manchester City have equalled the British transfer record with a £125m deal to sign Enzo Fernández from Chelsea, who were left raging after their attempts to replace the Argentina midfielder were dashed by Monaco reneging on an agreement to sell Lamine Camara on Tuesday night.

On a day of twists and turns, City emerged in a strong position after they bolstered their attack by signing Iliman Ndiaye from Everton for up to £65m and secured one of Enzo Maresca’s biggest targets on a five-year deal. Chelsea held out for a huge fee for Fernández and it seemed they were going to find a replacement for him as the transfer window drew to a close.

The club moved to agree a £47m fee with Monaco for Camara, who was poised to sign a six-year contract with the option of an extra year. Chelsea swooped when Everton’s attempts to sign the USA striker Folarin Balogun ran into difficulties. It left Monaco needing to raise funds from elsewhere, prompting Chelsea to revive their move for Camara after having a £38.1m offer for the 22-year-old Senegal midfielder rejected earlier in the day.

Chelsea had a written agreement with Monaco but were stunned by the Ligue 1 club pulling out of the deal as the deadline approached. Sources called Monaco’s conduct “deeply unprofessional”. As an extraordinary situation developed it emerged that Everton, who have also loaned Jack Grealish from City, had refused to give up on Balogun, renegotiating the fee for the former Arsenal forward only for that deal to also fall down just after midnight.

The collapse of Camara’s move did not lead to Chelsea cancelling the sale of Fernández to City. The deal means City have spent £327m on midfielders this summer following the arrivals of Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for £116m and Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille for £86m.

“I could not be happier to be here, and I am ready for the challenge of helping City continue winning trophies. This is a club built for success,” said Fernández, who becomes this country’s most expensive player alongside Alexander Isak, who joined Liverpool from Newcastle for £125m a year ago.

“I pride myself on continually improving my game. Anyone who’s worked with me will know how hard I train every single day and how much I put into matches. I give absolutely everything and I can promise Manchester City that will continue now I’m here.”

View image in fullscreen Iliman Ndiaye also completed his move to Manchester City on a busy deadline day for the club’s sporting director, Hugo Viana. Photograph: Manchester City FC

Maresca has a good relationship with Fernández after coaching him at Chelsea and a reunion has been on the cards for a while. City opened talks with Chelsea on Monday night and will feel they have successfully rebuilt their midfield after selling Rodri to Barcelona and losing Bernardo Silva to Real Madrid, while also selling Nico González to Newcastle. They were also not put off even after Chelsea’s unofficial deadline for clubs to lodge bids of £120m for Fernández passed last month.

Fernández has been angling for a way out of Chelsea since March and his departure was announced in a short statement on the club’s website. The 25-year-old, who scored 31 goals after joining from Benfica for £106.7m in January 2023, initially had his sights set on joining Real Madrid. He grew disillusioned following Maresca’s acrimonious split with Chelsea this year. Fernández, the unofficial vice-captain, spoke out after Chelsea were knocked out of the Champions League by Paris Saint-Germain in March. Chelsea responded by banning him for two games.

Fernández reported back to training after the World Cup and was booed by Chelsea fans during a pre-season friendly against Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge. He featured in the club’s opening first game of the season, coming off the bench to help Xabi Alonso’s side to beat Fulham, but was left out of Chelsea’s next two fixtures.

Chelsea came round to the view that a sale was in their interests. There is a feeling within the club that Fernández, who won the Conference League and Club World Cup during his time in west London, had not shown himself to be vice-captain material.

Chelsea have made in the region of £500m in loans and sales this summer. They finished the window by selling Marc Guiu to RB Leipzig for £16m and loaning Dário Essugo to Strasbourg, Robert Sánchez to Como and Mykhailo Mudryk to Tottenham. Tosin Adarabioyo joined Spurs on a permanent deal.

Sports.title: Everton left with only one striker after Balogun deal collapses late on deadline day
Sports.content:
Everton’s £40m move for US international Folarin Balogun collapsed late on deadline day to leave manager David Moyes with only one striker for the first half of the season.

Everton had agreed a £40m deal for Balogun only for issues with the striker’s medical to place the transfer in doubt after the Merseyside club had sold Beto to Fiorentina and Iliman Ndiaye to Manchester City. Enquiries were made to Manchester United for Joshua Zirkzee and Aston Villa for Tammy Abraham but proposed loans for both forwards were rejected.

The structure of the deal was renegotiated late on – Monaco accepted a lower payment up front and more in appearance related add-ons – and Everton submitted a deal sheet to complete the transfer in time. Balogun signed the squad sheet shortly before 11pm. But the 25-year-old, who is believed to have missed his scheduled morning flight to Merseyside and arrived later in the day, changed his mind over the move and walked away at the final moment. The collapse of the deal leaves Thierno Barry as Everton’s one recognised striker and completed a shambolic end to the window by the club’s hierarchy, who were already under pressure having tried to sell Harrison Armstrong to Nottingham Forest.

Everton also hit problems in their attempts to sign right-back Kenny Tete from Fulham. A £9m deal had been agreed for the defender only for Fulham to fail to land their preferred replacement, Andrei Ratiu of Rayo Vallecano. Everton finally concluded their long-running search for a right-back by signing former Arsenal player Ainsley Maitland-Niles from Lyon for a fee of around £4.2m. The 29-year-old has agreed a three year contract.

Funds were raised by the sales of Ndiaye to City, for £60m plus £5m in add-ons, Beto to Fiorentina for £15.5m, Tim Iroegbunam to Hull for an initial £15m and Nathan Patterson to Torino for an undisclosed fee.

Grealish returns to the Hill Dickinson Stadium on another season loan from City. The 30-year-old enjoyed a productive spell on loan in 2025-26 before sustaining a fractured foot that ended his campaign in February.

Grealish, who will be out of contract at City when this latest deal ends next summer, could make his second Everton debut against Manchester United on Sunday. He said: “I’m so happy. I think I’m at my best at everything in life, not just football, when I feel loved. That’s what the manager has given me, what my teammates have given me and especially what the fans have given me. Every time I see an Everton fan, it’s just pure love.

“It means a lot to me and hopefully I’ve made a few Everton fans happy. I had a perfect time here for the first six months, then I stayed around after I got injured. I’ve been watching all the Everton games in pre-season and since the season started. Now I feel ready to go.”

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Jamie Vardy to São Paulo or Sheffield Wednesday?
Sports.content:
Should have, would have, could have. Many fans will be using this phrase today after the Premier League transfer window closed at 11pm last night, meaning no more deals can but made until the winter window opens. Everton will be clawing at the glass like a cat who has seen a pigeon on the grass after a late deal for the USA international Folarin Balogun fell through.

The forward reportedly had his medical with the Toffees, which threw up an issue. Everton then went back to Balogun’s club, Monaco, to renegotiate and an agreement was reached with a deal sheet drawn up. But Balogun then decided against the move. It’s a blow to Everton, who have lost two attacking players this window, with Beto going to Fiorentina and Iliman Ndiaye signing for Manchester City.

Monaco were involved in another big deal that fell through late, on deadline day as Lamine Camara looked likely to join Chelsea. Two initial bids for the Senegal international were rejected but eventually the two clubs agreed a €55m (£47.1m) fee. The 22-year-old had a medical but after Everton came in for Balogun, who Monaco were more happy to sell, the club pulled out of the Camara-to-Chelsea deal. After Balogun to Everton fell through, Monaco could not then sell Camara as they did not sign the deal sheet before the window closed.

There are also whispers that Liverpool contacted Monaco to say they will make a move for Camara in 2027, with the Ligue 1 club perhaps believing that will involve a higher fee than the possible Chelsea deal.

Chelsea also enquired about Spanish midfielder Martin Zubimendi but Arsenal rejected any move for the 27-year-old. The Blues then batted off interest from Liverpool, who wanted to sign the France defender Malo Gusto on loan. Chelsea insisted on a permanent transfer.

Liverpool themselves blocked a deal for Cody Gakpo, who wanted a move to Manchester City. The forward reportedly held talks with Anfield bosses to clear the air after they denied the move.

Manchester United, meanwhile, are already planning a defensive restructure come next summer. It is thought Harry Maguire, Luke Shaw, Matthijs de Ligt and Lisandro Martínez are all on trial this season and they could potentially be replaced in 2027.

United may lose another player in coming days as Chido Obi wants a loan deal to a club in the Netherlands or Denmark. Both countries’ transfer deadlines are on Wednesday. It is thought Feyenoord are interested in the 18-year-old forward.

Wrexham are interested in Jamie Vardy but they are not the only one keen on the free agent: São Paulo and Sheffield Wednesday also want the 39-year-old. He played for Cremonese last season, and scored seven goals, but the club were relegated from Serie A, prompting the England international’s departure.

With that, our transfer-window watch ends. The Rumour Mill returns in January for plenty of hot gossip in (European) winter. Maybe some of the deals that might have been this summer will come to fruition then?

Sports.title: Football connects communities but can pull them apart if governed carelessly
Sports.content:
The fight for the soul of football isn’t just happening in the offices of Uefa and Fifa, it’s taking place on pitches much closer to home. At the weekend games of football for 750 children aged five to six in Scotland were cancelled due to severe behavioural issues within the ironically named “Fun 4s” programme. Seventy-two red cards were handed out in the first week of the season. Accounts describe adults displaying aggression, intimidation and head-butting as if it’s the “wild west”.

This isn’t just a Scottish problem. Contacts I speak to in different roles around football confirm and almost accept that “youth football is atrocious”. This should be sounding major alarm bells, for the consequences go way beyond the pitch. The existing disciplinary systems and PR campaigns are not nearly enough to address and change the situation.

It’s incredibly selfish and socially corrosive for an adult to intervene and spoil the experience of kids playing football. There are no good outcomes. For the children, they learn to associate football, and potentially life more broadly, with violence and aggression. They are robbed of a space to be free, to play and develop and have fun alongside their friends. They see adults role modelling a dog-eat-dog, win-at-all-costs mentality that is not laying the foundations for them to become good team players, school pupils or later civic-minded citizens. It also prevents young people from developing a love of being active and working positively in a team, perhaps one of the most powerful elements for a healthy life. It’s not a great way to develop parenting skills either.

There is no shortage of evidence about how important it is – whether you are trying to develop skilful football players or healthy young people – that children need space to play, try stuff out and thrive. We also know that it’s what children want from sport. Research by Amanda Visek at the Milken Institute of Public Health at George Washington University, confirms that when it comes to organised sport, kids just want to have fun. What counts for girls and boys are things like trying your best, working hard, playing well together as a team. When mapping 81 determinants of fun, “winning” ranked 40th in importance.

The Campaign for Children’s Rights in Football is an independent and impartial organisation. It’s preparing to launch and trying to create a greater platform for its work in the sport internationally. It’s needed more than ever.

The Centre for Young Lives set up the Raising the Nation Play Commission that published its report last year as part of a campaign for a national strategy to put play back into children’s lives. Last year the Scottish government published Scotland’s Play Vision Statement and Action Plan 2025-2030 to ensure that “every child is able to play across all stages and aspects of their life to support their social development, resilience, language and communication development, health, physical and mental wellbeing”. The Scottish FA had a “Let Them Play” campaign. But events playing out in Scotland show just how gaping the void is between government strategies, research and reality. This is going to take more than a communications campaign and a swathe of disciplinary proceedings. But investing in what is required for a deeper cultural change could create many positive ripples across our communities if the governing bodies get serious about making this their priority.

Creating thriving environments, ethics and focusing on the experience of those around you must become the first lesson in coaching training courses whether beginner or advanced. This needs to be the first part of training to be an official, or the conversation when your offer to volunteer is accepted by a local club. For any parents bringing their children to a club, clear standards, expectations and clarity on behaviours on and off the pitch should be integrated from the very first moment.

There is a bigger issue here. Sport is rightly cited as a great space to develop character, resilience, confidence. But that only happens in sports environments set up to develop those things. That wasn’t what was on offer on these Scottish youth football pitches. More sport may not help young people. Better experiences and environments will. That’s a crucial difference that has been missed when metrics have simply focused on growing participation and levels of activity.

Leadership is needed at the highest level. There’s a gap for our prime minister to call for sport to change itself in order to offer more to children and adults across the UK. When Andy Burnham called for “care to be at the heart of everything we do” that should include youth football and other sports experiences.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Elite football clubs have a responsibility, too, as key role models for how to play football. If there are things that happen in the Premier League that we wouldn’t want our children to emulate, we have to stop and ask why these things are happening at all. This question opens up a greater space for football to be a force for good. From their own talent-scouting interests, it’s also vital that future players are able to build on strong foundations of creativity, connection and strong intrinsic motivation – ie the love of the game, not just a love of winning.

Football and sport more widely have the power to unite a nation, to connect communities, to build positive solidarity. But we must also acknowledge, admit and understand that done poorly, without care, without strong leadership and clear cultural principles based on the experiences of all involved, it can pull apart the civic fabric we so desperately need to strengthen.

Sports.title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 12: Manchester United
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 7th (NB: this is not necessarily Tom Garry’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 4th

Prospects

It was all-change at Manchester United during pre-season, with the departure of their head coach Marc Skinner after five years followed swiftly by the appointment of Eva Olid as a new era begins. There have been significant outgoings from the playing group, including the senior squad members Melvine Malard, Gabby George, Millie Turner and Lisa Naalsund, as well as the end-of-contracts exits of Leah Galton and Hannah Blundell, but the signings of the Spain youth international defender Andrea Medina, the former Germany youth international goalkeeper Janina Leitzig and the Sweden forward Monica Jusu Bah will give the squad a fresh feel.

Missing out on the Women’s Champions League places by nine points last season was disappointing and after a summer in which other clubs have spent big, it feels more likely United will be looking over their shoulder at challengers coming up from fifth and sixth than mounting a title challenge.

Tottenham’s and London City’s ambitious recruitment mean they could threaten United’s position but United have not turned into a bad team overnight. European quarter-finalists last season, their squad retains a strong level of quality international players, despite the sale of Malard to Chelsea in particular. The England internationals Maya Le Tissier and Ella Toone are the senior leaders in a squad that also retains a world-class goalkeeper in Phallon Tullis-Joyce, the dynamic England midfielder Jess Park and the talented Sweden wing-back Anna Sandberg. A top-half finish feels realistic and the club will hope for strong runs in the domestic cups. There is also understood to be a desire at the club to make the playing style more entertaining for supporters.

Off-field picture

As with the men’s club, the Glazer family own a majority stake and Ineos – led by Sir Jim Ratcliffe – has a minority stake but has control of football operations. The women’s team’s financial history divides opinion in the sport; some argue United are an example of how to run a professional women’s team sustainably, having recorded a profit of £397,000 in their most recent accounts and a profit of £1.34m since reforming their senior women’s team in 2018, while others lament a lack of investment from the ownership compared with the budgets of their rivals such as Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester City.

The manager

Olid was appointed on 5 August on a two-year deal with the option of a further year. The Spanish coach, who turned 41 in late August, arrives after an impressive spell at Hearts, where she led the club to their first Scottish Women’s Premier League title in May. That made her the SWPL’s manager of the season. It is understood she was chosen by United’s hierarchy because they feel her CV demonstrates a strong track record of developing and improving young players.

Star signing

Bah, who has 11 caps, looks to be an important signing for United from BK Häcken for a fee reportedly of about £400,000. The 23-year-old helped the Swedish club win last term’s inaugural Women’s Europa Cup – European club-level women’s football’s second competition – and she said the opportunity to work with Olid was “perfect” because she wants to improve. She provided seven assists and scored 16 goals for her club last season and United will hope she can settle into the WSL quickly.

View image in fullscreen Monica Jusu Bah arrives in Manchester from Swedish club BK Häcken. Photograph: Poppy Townson/Manchester United/Getty Images

Stat attack

United made a mockery of underlying data last season. Only Arsenal overachieved against their attacking expected goals by more and only City conceded fewer compared with their xG at the back. They were ranked fourth for expected goal metrics at both ends but the combined variance of +9.86 against those numbers makes them hard to predict this season.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Set for a breakthrough

Layla Drury, an academy graduate, became United’s youngest player and goalscorer when given her debut in the Women’s FA Cup in January at 16, and this summer the 17-year-old became the youngest player to sign a professional contract with the club. She has been added to England’s Under-20 squad for September’s World Cup in Poland and last Saturday scored for the Young Lionesses in their 11-0 warm-up victory against New Caledonia. The forward had previously played for Wales’ youth teams.

What they say

“I always say: ‘My life is football.’ I don’t have other things. I spend probably 24 hours every day on football. It’s my life, my lifestyle and I give everything for the team and for the players. They always have me. Doubts, questions, [it] doesn’t matter the time of the day, I’m going to be there for them. I want to make them better, and that is how I’m going to feel good as a coach, seeing the improvement, seeing that they are better, and of course, winning matches” – Olid to MUTV.

Where are they playing their home games?

United play at Leigh Sports Village, a 12,000-capacity venue which is also the home of the rugby league club Leigh Leopards and United’s men’s Under-21s. It has been their home ground since 2018. The stadium hosted a quarter-final at 2022’s Euros. United’s final home WSL fixture, against Arsenal in May, has been scheduled for Old Trafford, although that match may have to be rearranged if Arsenal reach the semi-finals of the Women’s Champions League because the second legs are that weekend.

Sports.title: West Ham fight off Wolves as Divine Mukasa double eases pressure on Nuno
Sports.content:
It was a match between two disjointed sides, two teams trying to carve out new identities following the drop into the Championship. In the end West Ham won thanks to a bit of luck, a degree of resolve and, crucially, a sharpness in front of goal that took them away from Wolves and reduced the pressure on Nuno Espírito Santo, for a few days at least.

First-half goals from Divine Mukasa and Jarrod Bowen, the latter from the penalty spot, were complemented by two more in the second; Mukasa secured his brace alongside a goal for Konstantinos Mavropanos. The defender doubled up himself too, albeit by scoring at his own end, as Wolves tried to claw their way back into contention. The visitors also added a decent goal from the midfielder Marshall Munetsi to their tally. For all their obvious technical ability, however, César Peixoto’s side lacked the hosts’ sang-froid at the crucial moments and that proved the decisive factor.

Nuno’s mantra after the match was “I think we can do better”, but he was clearly grateful for the win. “We all know that it was much needed,” he said. “Looking back even on today, we have mistakes again but we’ve been much more effective in our attacking actions.”

With West Ham’s uncertainty extending beyond the field of play, there was much interest taken from the appearance of Amanda Staveley in the stands here. The former Newcastle shareholder remains in the running to acquire a stake in West Ham and could be seen punching the air at Mukasa’s first-half banger. The Manchester City loanee was not the only new recruit to impress, with Arne Engels excellent alongside him in midfield.

What gave off the vibes of being an uninspiring opening half ended up being blessed by three goals. West Ham were on the back foot for much of the opening half-hour but established a two-goal lead by the 40th minute after a short spell of improved play. The opening goal was a memorable one, hit by Mukasa from 25 yards and cannoning into the net off the underside of the bar. It was a memorable way for the teenager to open his account, and it came after a piece of smart attacking play that got Kyle Walker-Peters behind Wolves’ defensive line. Seven minutes later, Bowen converted a penalty after swift feet from Joel Piroe confused André into an untimely tackle.

View image in fullscreen Jarrod Bowen doubles West Ham’s lead from the penalty spot. Photograph: Saud Ahmed/PPAUK/Shutterstock

Before Nuno could get his troops into the dressing room and preach the importance of a clean sheet, Wolves hit back. With West Ham’s defence pushing up, a fortunate deflection off the previously bewildered André opened up the opportunity for Munetsi to run into space, check inside Mavropanos and finish coolly inside Mads Hermansen’s left-hand post.

With nascent enthusiasm tempered by the late concession, the atmosphere among the home support quietened as the second half began, perhaps in anticipation of further trials for West Ham. Instead they extended their lead in short order and it was Mukasa who struck again. This was a lovely move, starting with a cute through ball from Bowen that Pablo dummied to take four Wolves players out of the equation. Receiving on the edge of the box, Mukasa stood up Toti Gomes, shifted to his left and hit a shot that deflected off the Wolves skipper and beyond the despairing José Sá.

“I’m delighted by the way he played,” Nuno said of Mukasa. “All the young lads, not just those who joined this summer, have brought us energy and talent. There’s a lot of things to improve but I’m delighted to have him.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Wolves responded to the third goal by grabbing hold of possession once more, but the sprightly Fer López spurned two chances. Up the other end, however, and an Engels corner was deep and dangerous and, after Mavropanos saw a towering header crash off the bar, the Greek defender smashed the rebound home on the volley. Six minutes after celebrating, Mavropanos got the final touch to a cross from Jackson Tchatchoua to turn the ball into his own net.

Wolves created no further chances, but could take solace from the performance of the full-back Tchatchoua, who looked impactful at both ends, while Mateus Mané was dominant on the left. “We created a lot of chances to score, they scored more goals,” said Peixoto. “West Ham took their chances and that’s the difference.”

Sports.title: Sunderland pip Crystal Palace in battle of the private jets to land Malick Fofana
Sports.content:
Sunderland and Crystal Palace were involved in an extraordinary deadline-day tug of war that concluded with Malick Fofana agreeing to swap Lyon for the Stadium of Light in a club-record £31m move.

On Tuesday morning it had seemed that the 21-year-old Belgium winger was heading for Sunderland on a five-year contract, but then Pierre Sage led an attempt to hijack the deal. Palace’s manager coached Fofana at Lyon and forged a strong bond with a player he was keen to bring to Selhurst Park. After speaking to Sage on the phone, Fofana seemed to have changed his mind and decided he wanted to reunite with his old boss in south London. Sunderland, though, refused to surrender.

That meant Lyon had a bidding war on their hands and responded by agreeing improved deals with both clubs. Agents’ fees and Fofana’s personal terms were also understood to have risen accordingly. Meanwhile, two private jets, one dispatched by Sunderland and the other by Palace, sat on the tarmac at Lyon airport.

At one point Fofana was said to have been seen boarding the former aircraft before a flight to Newcastle airport but, in reality, he was headed to a private hospital in France for a medical commissioned jointly by Palace and Sunderland. With time running out, both clubs accepted this unusual arrangement was the only way a player targeted by Arsenal throughout much of the window would be heading to England.

In an attempt to remind Fofana, who scored 11 goals in 59 appearances for Lyon since arriving from Gent in 2024, why he had originally been so excited about playing for Régis Le Bris on Wearside, Kyril Louis-Dreyfus, Sunderland’s owner, flew to Lyon – presumably on a third jet – and spoke to him privately. It appears to have proved an inspired intervention as, shortly after 9pm, Fofana announced that he had made his choice and would be travelling to the Stadium of Light after all.

Although the initial fee agreed is £26m, add-ons dictate it should eventually rise to £31m. That leaves a forward capped five times by Belgium set to become Sunderland’s record signing, eclipsing the £30m paid to Strasbourg for midfielder Habib Diarra last summer. Sunderland have submitted a deal sheet and expect it to be concluded shortly.

Sports.title: Ismaila Sarr and Lamine Camara's furious agent accuses clubs of failing to 'respect African players' in astonishing attack after both stars fail to secure deadline day moves
Sports.content:
Ismaila Sarr and Lamine Camara's furious agent accuses clubs of failing to 'respect African players' in astonishing attack after both stars fail to secure deadline day moves

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The agent of Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr and Monaco's Lamine Camara has launched a scathing attack on football clubs after his players failed to secure a move on deadline day.

Sarr and Camara’s agent Diomansy Kamara, who previously played for Portsmouth, West Bromwich Albion and Fulham during his career, has accused clubs of treating African players as 'just a commodity' and failing to respect their ambitions.

Senegal international Sarr had hoped to secure a move away from Crystal Palace amid links to Liverpool and Galatasaray but ultimately finished the window at Selhurst Park, while Camara's £47million transfer to Chelsea collapsed at the 11th hour after Monaco pulled out of the deal.

Furiously speaking out on the failed transfers on Wednesday morning, Kamara posted on his Instagram story: 'The cases of Ismaila Sarr and Lamine Camara must all interrogate us.

'We have to get out of this logic where the African player can sometimes give the feeling that he is just a commodity: you buy it, you set its price, you negotiate its future and, too often, your will seems to go to the background.

'Our African players deserve respect. The respect of their work. The respect of their career. Respecting their ambitions. The respect of their voices.

The agent of Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr (left) and Monaco's Lamine Camara (right) has launched a scathing attack on clubs after his players failed to secure a move on deadline day

Agent Diomansy Kamara has accused clubs of treating African players as 'just a commodity'

'A transfer shouldn't just be a matter of two clubs and numbers. Behind every contract, there's a man, a career, dreams and life choices.

'The fact that clubs can sometimes have the final word is a reality of professional football. But one question remains: what about the career and the will of the player?

'The player must be able to be heard and respected in the decisions that determine his future.

'Let's never forget what's important: behind every success, it's the players who write history first.'

Camara's failed move to Chelsea became one of the main stories of deadline day as it left Xabi Alonso's side short in midfield following the British record departure of Enzo Fernandez for £125m to Manchester City.

Chelsea thought they had secured Camara from Monaco with less than two hours of deadline day remaining, having agreed a £47m deal.

Yet, in a dramatic twist, the Blues were left stunned and furious when Monaco then went back on their word as the 11pm deadline approached.

Chelsea sources say the two clubs had reached a full, written, club-to-club agreement for Camara to join. Yet when Monaco renegotiated their transfer of Folarin Balogun to Everton, Chelsea were told that the deal for Camara was being withdrawn.

Insiders at Stamford Bridge described it as a deeply unprofessional way for another club to conduct business.

Sports.title: The free agents that can still save Everton: David Moyes is left desperate for reinforcements after deadline day disaster
Sports.content:
Everton fans knew what they needed on deadline day. You'd like to think the board did too. Some full backs and a striker – it wasn't rocket science. It had looked as though Kenny Tete would join from Fulham to add to David Moyes's right back options, while Folarin Balogun was on his way to Merseyside for a medical to replace Beto, who had already departed. Former Arsenal – and England – star Ainsley Maitland-Niles signed in the afternoon. Nathan Patterson departed. Jack Grealish rejoined to replace Iliman Ndiaye. And all appeared to be going smoothly. That was until it wasn't. In spectacular – and, some would say, Everton fashion – Balogun performed a U-turn, Fulham pulled out of the Tete deal, and that was that. The Toffees now have only two recognised full backs, supported by others who can fill in, and one natural striker, with the transfer window closed. A disaster? Maybe. Enter the free agent market. Those who left clubs before the deadline closed can still join other sides, and the Toffees will almost certainly need to dip into that market. Here are some of the players who are still unattached that could help Moyes and Co this season. Everton have been left desperately short in terms of personnel following a disastrous final day of the transfer window Karim Benzema Definitely the most high-profile name on the list, Ballon d'Or and five-time Champions League winner Benzema would be an insane coup for the Toffees. Any arrival – if even possible – would come with caveats. He is 38 now, which is, for a better phrase, older than old- in football terms. A short-term deal wouldn't matter too much. There's no way Everton don't address the issue properly as soon as the next transfer window comes around, and Benzema could easily play second fiddle to Thierno Barry. His wages would likely be astronomically high. When he left Real Madrid for Al-Ittihad in 2023, he was reportedly earning a sensational £1.4million a week, then went onto pick up a cool £2million-a-week at Al-Hilal before his departure earlier this year. He would get nowhere near that at Everton – in fact he'd be looking at a huge pay cut. But is the challenge of the Premier League enough for that? It's unlikely. Karim Benzema would be a sensational signing for Everton, but may be an unrealistic target Oleksandr Zinchenko Zinchenko's career has fallen off a cliff since he left Arsenal last year. It felt a good move for all parties when he joined Nottingham Forest on a season-long loan in September 2025, but his time at the City Ground saw him make just ten appearances before his loan was cut short. He then moved to Ajax, but his contract expired after four months, and he remains unattached. A move for Everton doesn't seem like the worst idea in the world. Still only 29, Zinchenko has plenty of life left in his legs and has a lot of experience too. Let's remember he's a four-time Premier League winner, a four-time League Cup winner and a one-time FA Cup winner. This one seems plausible. Caveats include that he has played in midfield more regularly than at left back in recent years – and he's currently injured – but, if things fall into place, a move could make a lot of sense. Oleksandr Zinchenko's career has fallen off a cliff since he left Arsenal just last summer Raphael Guerreiro There aren't many free agent right backs for Everton to choose from, but there are a fair few left backs. And, with Jake O'Brien more than capable on the right but Jarrad Branthwaite probably second choice left back, that may not be a bad thing. Guerreiro may be past his prime but is still only 32 and left Bayern Munich in the summer. After three years there, plus seven at Borussia Dortmund, he would bring great experience and may even be happy to play back-up. That said, Everton fans are growing increasingly frustrated with Vitaly Mykolenko, and Guerreiro would certainly stake his claim for a starting spot. He could even be out of Everton's price range – but may well be worth a go. In desperate need of a left back, Everton could turn to out of contract Raphael Guerreiro Tyrell Malacia Malacia's Manchester United nightmare finally came to an end in the summer when he was released by the club after four years. Maybe Malacia wasn't ready for a club the size of United, but he is in his prime at 27 and undoubtedly hungry for a new challenge. A move back home to the Netherlands may be on the agenda following a stint at PSV last year, and he may not be keen to move back to the Premier League after such a nightmare experience the first time around. But, again, looking at the player and what Everton need... with Mykolenko the only recognised left back, a move would make sense. After his Manchester United nightmare, Tyrell Malacia may be reluctant to return to England Mauro Icardi Icardi has made more headlines off the field than on it in recent years. Long story short, he split from his high-profile spouse Wanda Nara, an Argentinian model and presenter with whom he has two kids, and accused her of infidelity – arguing she cheated on him with Argentinian singer L-Gante and former team-mates Federico Fazio and Keita Balde. You can read more by clicking here. On the field, he left Galatasaray in the summer after four years, and, at 33, is on the hunt for a new club. The striker is a prolific goal scorer and has been wherever he has gone: 124 in 219 games for Inter, 77 in 134 for Gala and 38 in 92 for PSG. But that may mean he isn't happy to be a back-up – though some healthy competition could work in Everton's favour. Moyes and Co may not feel he is worth the hassle. They would also have to move quickly, with it looking like he is set to join Lazio in Italy. A decent option from a footballing perspective, but one that feels almost impossible for Everton. Mauro Icardi is an option in attack but appears to be on the verge of joining Lazio in Italy Dani Carvajal Another player swimming in experience, former Real Madrid captain Carvajal is still yet to find a side after leaving Los Blancos in the summer. This one feels unlikely. He has played in Spain since 2013, and may not want to relocate to the Premier League at the age of 34. He was also on big wages at Madrid – a reported £171,000 a week. That wouldn't be on offer at Everton. Still, don't rule it out. Everton are a decent side playing in a top division and hoping to push for Europe. Unlikely, but never say never. Former Real Madrid captain Dani Carvajal is yet to find a new clb after leaving Los Blancos Anthony Martial Now now. Martial is remembered for all the wrong reasons in the Premier League. Announcing himself in style against Liverpool on his debut as a teenager, he's now 30, and has just left Mexican club Monterrey by mutual consent. Everyone remembers the Ballon d'Or clause in his contract when he joined United. And, to be frank, the situation went on to become a laughing stock. But it's important to look at the player in isolation. He has scored goals throughout his career. Martial netted 90 times in 317 games for United and nine in 24 for AEK Athens – though it is hard to ignore the one in 20 during his time in North America. Could he be worth a punt? Cheap wages, probably happy to play back-up, knows the Premier League... it would certainly split the fanbase. Former Manchester United striker Anthony Martial is still on the hunt for his latest club Joselu This is a man who was first choice striker for Real Madrid as little as 18 months ago, forming a surprise but effective partnership with Jude Bellingham. Now 36, a short-term move would suit all parties and Joselu's experience would likely prove more than handy in what has become a young Everton attack. He's a different type of striker, too – at 6ft 4in, his physical frame offers something Barry does not. After leaving Qatar side Al-Gharafa earlier this year, it was expected that he would join a new club in the summer. He hasn't, yet – and Everton could be the destination. Joselu could provide an option up front, having starred for Real Madrid as recently as two years ago Someone else? There aren't just full backs and strikers up for grabs. Any team can sign free agents outside the window, and there are plenty worth a look at. Some will surely find a side of sorts soon. Jadon Sancho is available, though seems to be on his way to Palmeiras in Brazil. Yves Bissouma hasn't found a new club after being released by Tottenham, and Reiss Nelson was let go by Arsenal before the window closed. Former Premier League stars Riyad Mahrez and Abdoulaye Doucoure are still available, too, along with the likes of Wilfried Zaha, Tanguy Ndombele, and a certain Raheem Sterling. The transfer window may well be closed. But for teams that failed to build their squads properly – such as Everton – hope is not lost.

Sports.title: Pakistan's chaotic England tour rumbles on: Opener Imam-ul-Haq faces probe after failing to bat at Lord's - as under-fire selector launches blistering attack and complains: 'The world is laughing at us'
Sports.content:
Pakistan's chaotic England tour rumbles on: Opener Imam-ul-Haq faces probe after failing to bat at Lord's - as under-fire selector launches blistering attack and complains: 'The world is laughing at us'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Imam-ul-Haq will be subject to a disciplinary probe from Pakistan after failing to bat in either innings of last week's series-deciding defeat to England at Lord's.

Imam suffered a calf tear early in the 194-run Test loss, but is set to have action taken against him, according to Pakistan director of high performance Aaqib Javed, who also doubles as one of his country's selectors.

Aaqib blasted the former Yorkshire left-hander in an interview with Pakistani television network Geo, adding to an extraordinary few days that has seen seven players axed, Sarfaraz Ahmed sacked as Test coach and Misbah-ul-Haq resign from the selection committee.

'The Imam injury is a big question mark, and a deep disappointment,' Aaqib said.

'Players in the past used to get injuries, but they used to put on casts (to play) and still tried. We'll take action against this.

'How is it possible that a pulled muscle ruled you out of batting in both innings? He should have tried and fought. He'll have to face an inquiry; I can't say he faked it, but a muscle pull like that cannot stop you from batting altogether.'

Imam-ul-Haq will be subject to a disciplinary probe from Pakistan after failing to bat at Lord's

Shortly before play began on the second morning, the Pakistan Cricket Board issued a statement revealing the 30-year-old nephew of the legendary Inzamam-ul-Haq had suffered a tear in his left calf, and that medical advice would determine his further participation in the match.

Two days later, having not batted in Pakistan's first innings effort of 110 all out, Imam emerged to warm-up alongside his team-mates, but was criticised by Sky Sports commentator Stuart Broad, who reckoned it was 'all for show.'

Imam did not bat later that day, with Shan Masood deputising as opener once again as an Ollie Robinson-inspired England dismissed the tourists for 194.

Hours later, it emerged that Imam was one of a septet of players being sent home that also included established wicketkeeper Mohammad Rizwan, Salman Agha, who had captained the side in the first Test in Babar Azam's absence and then been dropped for the second, and Ali Usman, who took a five-wicket haul at Headingley.

'Two Test matches have come and gone and the team has not competed in any way,' Aaqib said, appearing to blame Sarfaraz and Babar for picking the wrong XI.

'There's one Test still to go. They [the management] had a pace all-rounder available, a second wicketkeeper, a fast bowler in Ubaid Shah. But those decisions were not being made. I spoke to the captain and coach and asked them to put Ubaid in because the other bowlers are all similarly paced.

'No batter in our top seven bowls. We should have included an allrounder, but most importantly, get in Ubaid Shah. One fast bowler changes the composition of your attack.

'I understand dropping Agha, who's out of form, but you should have played Ghazi Ghori instead of Rizwan. Someone had to take action. The world is laughing at us because we can't even compete. The message we're sending to the recalled players is that you have to raise your game on important tours and compete, and we should be able to see some effort.'

The Imam investigation arguably deflects from Aaqib's own role in Pakistan's demise over the past two years.

Highly-respected foreign coaches Jason Gillespie and Gary Kirsten considered their positions untenable after just a few months and Aaqib, after a failed stint as head coach himself, was influential in appointing Sarfaraz in May.

Of his own involvement in picking the touring party for this three-match series, Aaqib said: 'When we select the team as coach or captain and make a squad, we're responsible for that squad.

'But once they go on tour, we cannot do anything about the match-to-match combination.

'No one doubted these players' performances when selected. But when players are completely out of form and you're not competing at all, then we needed to make a decision.

'Your captain, head coach and management have some responsibilities.'

Sports.title: Record-breaking numbers behind the transfer window: Chelsea splash out £342m and STILL make the most money, two promoted teams sit in the top five for net spend - and it's another expensive summer for Liverpool
Sports.content:
Liverpool had the highest net spend in a record-breaking summer transfer window for Premier League clubs.

Top-flight teams have splashed the cash over recent months, surpassing last season's spending record of £3billion, and the Reds have led the way.

Andoni Iraola's side brought in the likes of Jeremy Jacquet, Victor Munoz, Lucca Brughmans and Bradley Barcola for big money fees - including a £123million deal for the French forward - while they only shifted Curtis Jones (£30m to Inter Milan) and Luca Stephenson (£700,000 to Bolton) for cash.

That put their net spend at £219.4m, just ahead of newly-promoted Ipswich's £190.7m.

The Tractor Boys, now managed by Gary O'Neil, added 14 senior additions and broke their transfer record first with Brazilian forward Emersonn (£24m from Toulouse) before they surpassed that with the addition of Julio Enciso (£26.1m from Strasbourg).

Meanwhile, Tottenham's heavy spending has been well documented, with Roberto De Zerbi's side shelling out £334m on the likes of Mateus Fernandes, Savio, Omar Marmoush and Sandro Tonali.

Premier League clubs broke the record for the most money spent in a transfer window this summer, with 11 sides breaking their own record for a player signing

Liverpool had the highest net spend after bringing in the likes of Bradley Barcola for £123m

Fernandes became Spurs' record signing (£85m from West Ham) before Tonali's arrival for £100m from Newcastle ensured the Italian took that mantle.

However, they did recoup £158m in sales through the likes of Cristian Romero (£34m to Atletico Madrid), Luka Vuskovic (£50m to Brighton) and Djed Spence (£30m to Inter Milan).

Spurs were the third highest spenders in the window, with Man City having the largest outlay at £440.3m.

That included three mega-money additions in midfield via record signing Enzo Fernandez (£125m from Chelsea), Elliot Anderson (£116m from Nottingham Forest) and Ayyoub Bouaddi (£86m from Lille).

They also signed Iliman Ndiaye (£65m from Everton).

However, Enzo Maresca's side managed to recoup £314.9m through sales.

The exits of Savio (£85m to Tottenham), Rodri (£65.4m to Barcelona), Nico Gonzalez (£50m to Newcastle) and James Trafford (£40m to Leeds) meant their net spend was only the sixth-largest at £125.4m.

The second-highest spenders were Chelsea at £342.4m but the Blues managed to bring in £409.7m in player sales, the most of anyone, to give them the lowest net spend of -£67.3m.

Morgan Rogers came in as a record arrival from Aston Villa for £117m, while Maxence Lacroix (£51m from Crystal Palace), Marco Palestra (£43m from Atalanta) and Pep Chavarria (£16.3m from Rayo Vallecano) were among other major signings.

Those funds were recouped though through the exits of Enzo Fernandez (£125m to Man City), Nicolas Jackson (£65m to Aston Villa), Marc Cucurella (£51.8m to Real Madrid) and Andrey Santos (£50m to Man United).
